#1912. Man City: Why the international break could be vital for Maresca

By Axel Clody | 16 Nov 2026 06:59

Manchester City began the season with the impression that adapting to Enzo Maresca’s work would be quick. With seven wins in the opening Premier League rounds, the team took the lead and at one point opened up a six-point advantage over Arsenal. The run, however, was abruptly interrupted.

Defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest dropped the team to third place and allowed the current champions to pull clear at the top.

More than the scorelines, the performances exposed difficulties in competing physically, winning duels and protecting the defence when possession is lost. Maresca himself acknowledged that his team could not keep up with the intensity of the opposition in the first half.

So the November international break comes at a good time. The pause will not erase the problems that have appeared in recent weeks, nor does it mean that all the players will have days off. But it offers the manager a valuable opportunity to assess performance, recover players and work on adjustments that would hardly be possible with a run of matches.

The drop in City’s level cannot be explained only by a lack of efficiency in front of goal.

The team can still control possession and produce offensive volume. Against Forest, for example, it finished the game with 79 per cent possession and 12 shots. The problem is that this control has not been enough to stop opponents finding space and creating dangerous situations.

One of the main issues is defensive protection. City have conceded 17 goals in eight matches and have not kept a clean sheet in any of their last nine games. The high defensive line, a hallmark of Maresca’s teams, demands coordination between the units and a quick ability to react to losing the ball. When the counter-press does not work, the defenders are left exposed to fast attacks and have to defend large spaces.

The absence of Rodri helps to explain part of this difficulty. The Spaniard offered reading of the game, interceptions and the quality to organise the build-up. More than a defensive midfielder who protects the defence, he is a player capable of anticipating danger and stopping counter-attacks before they gather speed. Without him, the rest of the midfield has to share responsibilities that Rodri used to take on almost alone.

Elliot Anderson has been important in this context, but so too is the distribution of roles. The presence of players such as Enzo Fernandez and Rayan Cherki adds technical quality and creativity, but also demands defensive cover. If the two play together without a structure that protects the central area, Anderson can be overburdened in covering and in physical duels.

The break allows Maresca to work on these relationships. One possibility is to adjust the make-up of the midfield, ensuring more balance between creation and protection. Another is to review the team’s positioning without the ball, especially the distance between the defensive line and the most advanced players. It is not necessarily a question of abandoning the style of play, but of finding ways to make it less vulnerable.

The calendar and the physical condition of the squad are another important aspect. City lost rhythm during a demanding period of fixtures, and the recovery of players can help the team regain the intensity needed to execute Maresca’s model.

It will also be important to monitor the situation of Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol. Both were substituted at half-time against Nottingham Forest because of physical problems, according to Maresca. The break could be useful to assess the extent of the issues and avoid important players returning before they are fully fit.

There is, however, a caveat: the international break is not a holiday for the whole squad. Several starters have been called up by their national teams, among them Erling Haaland, Gianluigi Donnarumma, Ruben Dias, Gvardiol, Guehi, Enzo Fernandez and Cherki. Travel and international commitments reduce the recovery time for some players, while others will be able to stay in Manchester and work directly with the coaching staff.

Even so, the break offers an opportunity to reorganise the workload and prepare the squad for what follows. In a season in which intensity is essential to the functioning of Maresca’s system, managing physical wear and tear is also part of the recovery process.

The break arrives at a time when City need to recover not only results, but also confidence in their own way of playing. The seven opening wins showed that the team has the resources to compete for the title. The three defeats that followed, on the other hand, revealed that there are still important adjustments to be made to sustain that level over an entire season.

The first challenge after the break will be against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. Then the team will face an even more significant fixture: the visit to Arsenal on 29 November. The six-point gap makes the direct meeting an important opportunity to close the distance, although the result will not be enough, by itself, to settle the title race.

For Maresca, the international break is a chance to find answers before the run of negative results turns into an even bigger problem. The manager needs to restore defensive solidity, find the best distribution of roles in midfield and make possession dominance translate into effective control of matches again.

City do not need to abandon their identity to react. Above all, they need to find a better balance between what they do with the ball and what they can do when they lose it. If the break allows Maresca to progress with this work and recover important players, the team could return better prepared to face a decisive stretch of the season.

#1910. The Brugge issue and a familiar backstory: Why the Tresoldi deal is becoming off-putting

Recently, it’s felt like AC Milan have been set on signing Nicolo Tresoldi in the winter. It may be the easy option, but is it the right one?

At a time when Milan are doing the PR side of things almost perfectly, Tresoldi feels like another easy win. It seems increasingly likely that Francesco Camarda departs in the winter mercato, so why not replace him with another Milanista?

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, if the Rossoneri came knocking, would he be able to say no to his boyhood club?

Well, here is the alternative view: maybe they shouldn’t knock at all.

Now, it’s unpopular to suggest that Tresoldi isn’t the right man, but stick with us here, especially after reports today. If you’ve not seen, Club Brugge have made a statement in the Belgian outlet Het Laatste Nieuws that they won’t be selling him in January.

It’s a ‘club policy’ and even for €60-70 million, he won’t be leaving Belgium. We’ve seen these kinds of statements become pointless in the past and this could become one of them. However, that’s not really the important thing here.

Instead, it’s that Tresoldi has now entered a new bracket. €50m in January is steep, but it’s workable. Ultimately, we’re not in record-breaking territory. Taking that €10-20m step upwards, though, that’s where we enter that territory. There’s also a possibility that more would be needed, too.

It’s a figure that Gerry Cardinale may not be afraid to spend. In fact, reports would have you believe that he really loves Tresoldi and sees him as a perfect addition to a strong frontline roster. However, that’s a lot of money on two strikers in one season.

Then, you’ve also got negotiations with Brugge to deal with. Historically, the Diavolo have found it difficult to close deals with them and with Tresoldi, it’ll be harder than ever, especially after the Ardon Jashari situation.

With the figures being discussed too, you can only imagine how small the margins will be.

Then, you have maybe the most difficult factor. Tresoldi, taking romanticism out of it, has only performed in, with respect, sub-tier leagues. Now, that’s not to take away from his records; scoring-wise, he’s been phenomenal and he’s matched it in the Champions League.

However – and it’s a big however – we’ve already seen that it doesn’t always translate. For example, look at Charles De Ketelaere, but that’s not the real parallel here.

Here, we head to the parallel. In the summer just gone, Milan hired a new Portuguese coach, who initially faced a few questions. After an up-and-down first half of the season, they find themselves in need of a statement January window and stumble upon a boyhood fan of the Rossoneri.

Said fan is banging goals in for fun in a league outside of Europe’s top five, but there’s no need to panic as he’s performing in the Champions League, even against the biggest teams. So, the Rossoneri make the plunge.

Six months later, they try to sell him and a year after that, he’s on loan at Porto, with an €18m buy clause sitting in his deal, unlikely to be touched. Of course, that’s Santiago Gimenez.

There are differences between them, of course, but the formula has already been tried and the results speak for themselves. Trying it again, whilst enticing for the same romantic reasons as Gimenez’s arrival, may not be the answer.

Yes, Gimenez had issues with selection and injuries and eventually, both together. Nevertheless, even without these problems, it was a rushed deal and the Diavolo are going to be the ones paying for that rush next season.

The point here isn’t to discredit the Mexican, but rather suggest that rushing to sign a romantic connection isn’t always the best way to spend big money. It’s about balance, which is why another striker signing like Nicolas Füllkrug wouldn’t be ideal.

Denying that Tresoldi could become a great would be naive, but it would also be as bad to ignore the reasons why the deal is becoming more of a gamble. At €50m, it makes sense, but we’re entering an echelon of deals that requires serious consideration.

In January, Milan would probably have to spend upwards of €70m and that wouldn’t guarantee them Champions League football. Nothing really will offer complete assurances in football; few things – if anything – are guaranteed. Yet, for that fee, it would be expected and you’re still not really addressing the issues within the squad completely.

To do that, Cardinale would have to spend at least another €30-40m to satisfy the fanbase and that’s unreasonable halfway through a season.

So, diversifying the money across the team and then reassessing in the summer may be the best route forward. After all, with this increased price demand, you’re hardly going to be paying more in the summer – and if their demands reach that amount, you’re voicing new questions.

With Markus Krösche also coming in, the January mercato will be one where everything has to be considered carefully and judgements will be made before February 1 rolls around. Spending so heavily on one target may also be an early and unnecessary strike on his record, if it doesn’t work.

For many, Tresoldi made sense in January because he’d be an investment at an investment price. Now, you’re looking at a major budget depletion for a striker who has yet to become a senior international and/or a regular goalscorer in one of Europe’s top five leagues.

The romantic side of it is great; it’s difficult not to fall for that. Financially, though, signing Tresoldi is becoming a tougher sell and that’s where we might have to start listening to the brain rather than the heart.

#1909. Ryan Porteous reckons people are still reading too much into THAT red card against Germany that made him a pariah with Tartan Army

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 17:47 EST, 11 November 2026

From a distance, it was difficult not to look at the fall-out from Ryan Porteous’ rash challenge on Ilkay Gundogan in the opening match of Euro 2024 and draw sweeping conclusions.

Coming on the cusp of half-time in the Allianz Arena, the defender’s two-footed lunge on the German midfielder earned him a straight red card with a two-game suspension soon following.

The moment of madness led to Kai Havertz giving the host nation a three-goal lead from the penalty spot at the interval. By time-up, Steve Clarke’s depleted side had lost 5-1. The self-belief which they’d brought into the tournament was fast evaporating, too.

While no one doubted the scale of the task Scotland faced before a ball was kicked that evening, Porteous’ actions made the mission impossible. As a consequence, the former Hibernian defender found forgiveness hard to come by.

Those irate Scotland supporters who demanded that he suffered for his folly were granted their wish.

A player who’d featured in seven of the eight qualifiers disappeared from view thereafter, briefly emerging from international exile as a sub against Greece in March of last year, yet posted missing again throughout the World Cup qualifiers and from the tournament itself.

Ryan Porteous' red card gave Scotland a mountain to climb in Euro 2024 defeat to Germany

It seemed only logical to deduce that Clarke had also shared the anger of the Tartan Army and that the player’s status as a pariah was down to his simmering fury at the humiliation that woeful tackle caused.

Porteous always believed the matter wasn’t quite as clear cut as most imagine it to be.

‘I think people maybe read too much into that,’ said the 27-year-old.

‘In the conversations I had with Steve after the Euros and in the next qualifying campaign, the red card against Germany never came up.

‘We had loads of conversations, both when I was in and out of the squad.

‘Those are the things that people obviously don’t see.

‘They maybe think Steve Clarke is the type of person who wouldn’t phone you or text you. But he did. We spoke loads to be honest. He was really honest with me.

‘I texted him when he left the role and he messaged back eager to see me get back in the squad.

The Scotland defender was shown a straight red for this challenge on Ilkay Gundogan

‘Everyone knows Steve is a manager who, if he picks a squad and they do well for them and they get to a tournament, he’s loyal.

‘In terms of the conversations we had during those latter stages of qualification, he just told me to keep doing what I was doing.

‘He was honest and told me I would probably need some of those lads to drop off in form if I was going to make it. You have to respect that.

‘I went to a tournament in the Euros in 2024 and you had someone like John Souttar who missed out. So, I know what it feels like on both sides.’

Porteous, to his credit, doesn’t appear to be bitter about how matters unfolded post-Germany.

Regardless of the true importance of the red card in his status changing from mainstay to that of an outcast, he accepts that fairness and the game do not always walk hand-in-hand.

‘That happens in football, it’s just one of those things,’ he shrugged.

‘I’ve had a career where I’m up and down, I’m left and right, you just need to bounce back from it.

‘It was a fantastic experience for me to be part of that run we went on. It helped me grow massively. I don’t look at it as being unfair.’

Porteous has now returned from period in wilderness ahead of North Macedonia clash

By the time he’d moved from Watford to Los Angeles to sign for LAFC last August, he’d already reconciled himself with the fact that his Scotland career was in cold storage. The consolation was that this afforded him a different perspective on the November night when history was made.

‘It’s maybe tough when the squads were getting announced and then a couple of days after that,’ he reflected.

‘But then as soon as you’re watching the games, you just become a fan straight away again and want the team to do well.

‘I probably hadn’t experienced that for a while. It was actually good for me watching the World Cup qualifiers - because I was able to sit and watch them straight after training because of the time difference.

‘When Kenny McLean scored from the halfway line (against Denmark) I had half the team in LA shouting and screaming for Scotland! It was brilliant.’

While he’d clearly have preferred to still have been at the heart of things, his new life on the other side of the Atlantic allowed him to sample what it all meant to an invading army in the summer.

‘I had a few days off at one point and I went out to Boston,’ he explained.

‘I didn’t manage to go to the games, but I saw my friends and family who were over and we went to the baseball as well.

‘Being in that fan environment, it just gives you that extra little bit of hunger to get back.’

Porteous in action for Scots at training as they prepare for North Macedonia showdown

The profile of the MLS always offered him that possibility. Porteous’s club counts Gareth Bale and Olivier Giroud among its former players. Son Heung-min is the current star in Tinseltown. The Scot played against - and defeated - Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami in February. In such moments, one can feel a long way from Midlothian.

‘I think I could be the first guy ever to go from Dalkeith to LA! It’s very hot. They are actually choking for a bit of rain just now.

‘I used to blame the East Mains wind for losing my hair, but it’s still falling out over in LA even without the wind.

‘(John) McGinn has already peppered me after seeing a couple of my interviews over there.

‘I’ve had to change my accent so that people can understand me over there.

‘For the first couple of months, everyone was asking me to repeat myself. But it’s an incredible place and I’m enjoying every second.’

LAFC finished sixth in the Western Conference this year, good enough to book a slot in the forthcoming play-offs.

Porteous’ part in that meant he was firmly in Sebastien Pocognoli’s thoughts when Stephen Welsh suffered an untimely injury ahead of the two final Nations League matches.

Over two years on from that hideous night in Munich, this feels like a deserved opportunity to change the narrative which has surrounded him ever since.

‘People pay their money and they can have their opinions on me,’ he said.

‘I’ve got thick skin now. It’s never been an issue for me in terms of managers having to pull me aside and have a word or anything like that.

‘I’m in a good place now. Whatever criticism I get, it only makes me grow stronger as a person.

‘Hopefully, I can come back now a better player than what people saw before.

‘I have still got my strengths and I feel like I’ve added to my game as well from being in different leagues and different environments.’

#1908. Thomas Tuchel speaks out on James Trafford vs Jordan Pickford battle for England spot

Thomas Tuchel insists that England do not have a number one, after James Trafford made a brilliant case to be first choice goalkeeper in the win over Spain.

Trafford played the full game as the Three Lions pulled off a memorable 3-2 Nations League win over the world champions in Madrid.

It was a stunning first hour from Tuchel’s side and the visitors were 3-0 up on 57 minutes thanks to goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

Things started to unravel a bit from there as Elliot Anderson was shown a straight red card and Mikel Oyarzabal converted from the penalty spot.

Nico Williams then made it a very nervy climax for England as he scored on 75 minutes and the hosts pushed for an equaliser.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Trafford helped his team stand firm, though, including making a tremendous double save late on.

Everton’s Jordan Pickford has been first choice goalkeeper since 2018, winning 94 caps, but his place is now in doubt thanks to the emergence of Trafford.

James Trafford last-gasp double save 🤯🤯#UNLSaves | @Betano_PT pic.twitter.com/K3Rn995OEE

Tuchel was not ready to declare either stopper his number one, but was clearly very impressed by the Leeds United star.

‘There’s no number one,’ said the England boss. ‘It’s a good double save. That’s what we wanted. He had a brilliant match. It only works if you’re top from number one to 11.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Tuchel continued on Trafford: ‘Very good. That’s his job, to close the gap. We want competition in all positions. We need to see Trafford in high-pressure moments.

‘The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end. Absolutely brilliant.’

The German has also liked what he has seen from Trafford on the ball, saying: ‘There was a lot to do in the deep build-up as well, which he did very, very well, with everyone around him.

‘Never lose the concentration, never lose the focus, never lose the vision where to find the free men to overcome the press and put the game to the opponent’s half.

‘With everyone else, he was part of a fantastic team performance.’

At 24 years old, Trafford is eight years younger than Pickford and looks to be his successor, even if he has not entirely displaced him just yet.

The win in Spain meant England topped their Nations League group and will play a runner-up from another group in the quarter-finals of the competition.

Groups A2 and A4 come to an end on Monday and Tuesday respectively, which is when we will learn England’s possible opponents for Friday’s draw.

Belgium have already secured second place in group A1, so they are a possible opponent for the Three Lions in the quarter-finals that are played in March next year.

#1907. Man Utd told Chelsea star would be ‘good signing’ for Mauricio Pochettino

Mikael Silvestre has encouraged Manchester United to explore a move for Estevao – but doubts the forward could be coaxed to the Theatre of Dreams as he appears intent on ‘fighting for his place’ at Chelsea.

United spent in the region of £160million on new signings in the summer, with club chiefs showing they were prepared to back Michael Carrick following an impressive third-place finish.

But any optimism that had grown amongst the fanbase in the back-end of last season rapidly faded as a 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea last month extended the Red Devils’ miserable winless run to nine matches in all competitions.

A stunning comeback victory over Roma followed by a 4-4 thriller at home to Aston Villa in the Premier League were ultimately not enough to save Carrick, who was relieved of his duties last Thursday.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach Mauricio Pochettino was subsequently announced as Carrick’s successor, with the Argentine officially vacating his position with the United States national team to start life in the role later this week.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Naturally, attentions have quickly turned towards the January transfer window, when United will be expected to splash the cash in the hope of boosting their prospects for the second half of the campaign.

United chiefs are set to resurrect their pursuit of a left-back as a priority to provide support for Luke Shaw after missing out on Newcastle’s Lewis Hall in the summer.

It’s understood the Old Trafford giants will also be in the market for attacking reinforcements on the back of a desperately disappointing start to the season for the likes of Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko.

According to Silvestre, Chelsea winger Estevao could represent a ‘good signing’ for United, with the Brazilian having made just one start in the Premier League under Xabi Alonso.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

That start happened to come against United, though, and the 19-year-old was widely praised for his performance as goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer proved decisive at Stamford Bridge.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Well, Estevao played against United for Chelsea, and I think he’s shown why he should feature more,’ Silvestre told Betarades.gr.

‘It looks like he’s going to fight for his place in the team, so I don’t anticipate United making a move for him.

‘But he’s a good player for sure. He’s playing for the national team of Brazil, and I like his style. If he were available, he would be a good signing for United.’

Asked why Newcastle and England star Hall may ‘make sense’ for United at left-back, Silvestre replied: ‘Lewis Hall had an impressive season with Newcastle, and he’s been on the club’s radar for sure.

‘The club made an attempt to sign him and other fullbacks, but couldn’t get it done.

‘They now have to rely on Luke Shaw, Diego Dalot, on Noussair Mazraoui, and on Patrick Dorgu, who has also been injured for quite some time. So that’s not been helpful either.’

Another high-profile name heavily linked with United in recent weeks has been Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has scored five goals in his opening nine appearances for Leeds this term.

But Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with the Red Devils, believes the England striker would only be brought in as a stop-gap for his former club up front.

‘I think Dominic Calvert-Lewin would be a stop-gap,’ the ex-United and France defender explained.

‘I don’t think it’s a long-term. He doesn’t belong in a Manchester United squad. So I don’t know where this is coming from.

‘Yes, you need to have a look around for strikers because of the Sesko situation with his injury, and we are short in that department, but I wouldn’t consider Calvert-Lewin as an option.’

All eyes will be on Anfield on Sunday when Pochettino takes charge of United for the first time against bitter rivals Liverpool.

Pochettino takes over the reins from Carrick with the club languishing down in 18th place in the Premier League, just point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

#1906. Mikel Arteta faces huge Arsenal injury blow as key £55m star hobbles off on international duty

By Lewis Blain | 16 Nov 2026 07:01, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 07:11

Arsenal have been handed an injury scare after Martin Zubimendi was forced off during Spain's defeat to England on Sunday evening.

The Gunners midfielder appeared to suffer a hamstring problem in the second half at the Metropolitano Stadium, prompting Luis de la Fuente to replace him with Nico Williams.

The extent of the problem remains unclear, but his availability for the north Londoners' upcoming fixtures is surely now a concern for manager Mikel Arteta.

Zubimendi's evening took a disappointing turn after he was forced off with an apparent hamstring injury during La Roja's 3-2 defeat to the Three Lions in the UEFA Nations League.

Spain had initially fallen three goals behind following strikes from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White, before attempting to mount a comeback after Elliot Anderson's red card.

However, the £55m Arsenal midfielder was unable to continue, with Athletic Club winger Williams introduced in his place.

The injury will concern Arteta, particularly with Arsenal facing a demanding schedule as the campaign heads towards the festive period.

It remains too early to establish how long Zubimendi could be sidelined, but an extended absence would put his participation in several important fixtures in doubt.

Arsenal are scheduled to face Newcastle United away in the Premier League, Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League and title rivals Manchester City before the end of the month, meaning the 27-year-old could miss a significant run of matches if the injury proves serious.

Any lengthy absence for Zubimendi would be a frustrating development for Arteta, who needs as many of his key players available as possible during an increasingly busy period.

The festive schedule is approaching, with domestic and European commitments leaving little room for the manager to rest his first-choice players.

Although Declan Rice has continued to impress, losing another midfield option would reduce Arteta's flexibility when rotating his squad and managing workloads.

Zubimendi has not always enjoyed the game time he might have expected following his arrival in 2025, but that does not diminish his importance as a squad option.

Arsenal will now hope the injury is relatively minor and that the midfielder can return quickly, so until the extent of the problem is established, his availability for the upcoming fixtures must remain a concern.

#1905. Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

“I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

“But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

“But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a new British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

In this scrupulously detailed account of Arsenal’s summer, Sam Dean assesses where things went right, and wrong, for the Premier League champions in the transfer market.

They have buttressed the two areas in which they were already strong by signing Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa, but failed to sign the level-raising forward Mikel Arteta coveted.

In fact, with Gabriel Jesus, Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli departing (as well as Ethan Nwaneri moving on loan), their weakest department is arguably weaker than this time last year. Christos Tzolis, signed for £34m from Club Brugge, is their only attacking purchase.

But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.

I want to thank every single one of you: the staff, the coaching team, the medical team, the physios, and everyone who works at Cobham and throughout this great institution.

To all my teammates over these years, thank you from the bottom of my heart for sharing so many moments with me. I was truly happy here, and I wish you nothing but the very best for the future.

Thank you for all the love and support you have given me and my family throughout these years. I will never forget it.

This group will give you many more reasons to be happy, and I will be happy for you too. Never doubt that.

You will always be in my heart, Blues. I will always wish you, always, nothing but the very best.

I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

Jack Grealish to Everton is done. A small gathering of fans are waiting outside Finch Farm, the club’s training base, but the calmness of this little road, will be at odds with the scrambling that is going on behind closed doors.

Zirkzee is staying at United. No move to Everton. United want the cover in attack and Everton’s approach happened too late with no chance of replacing him.

Crystal Palace have agreed a deal to re-sign Ben Chilwell. The 29-year-old was on loan at Palace last year and deal struck with Strasbourg for him to leave French club and return to the Premier League.

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

Mykhailo Mudryk’s loan move from Chelsea to Spurs has been confirmed.

Forgive the personal opinion but this is my favourite deal of the window. Mudryk played some of his best football under Roberto De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk. The Spurs head coach has even described Mudryk as “my son”, and has previously tipped him as a future Ballon d’Or winner.

After so long out of the game, Mudryk now has a coach who knows exactly how to get the best out of him. It might not work at all. Mudryk may need months to rediscover his match sharpness after so long out. But I am very excited to find out.

Iliman Ndiaye has been confirmed as a Manchester City signing. He moves on a five-year deal from Everton with the deal worth £65m.

The fee means Premier League spending has now surpassed the previous record for a summer window which stood at £3.14bn. The running tally now stands at £3.193bn.

Ndiaye says: “I’ve worked my whole life for an opportunity like this. City are one of the best clubs in the world and I’ve seen them win everything as I’ve grown up.

“It’s not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I’m here. It feels so good.

“I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That’s why I know this is the perfect fit.

“City fans can rest assured that I will give my all to bring more success to this incredible club.”

Chelsea had been holding off from sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City while they searched for a new midfielder of their own.

But City’s willingness to agree a £125m package has convinced Chelsea to give the green light to the Fernández move without any guarantees over an incoming signing.

Chelsea still have a few hours to try to make something happen, having had a bid for Lamine Camara turned down.

But Chelsea ultimately felt they had no choice but to let Fernández, who made it clear he wanted to leave, go in the best interests of the club.

Chelsea believe they have a strong squad, regardless of whether or not a new player is signed today, and will continue to weigh up their options.

The medicals are under way for Jack Grealish, Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Folarin Balogun at Everton but there is no clarity on when all three deals will be concluded. It must be stressed that no issues are envisaged and they will be the only additions to the squad before the window closes. Fulham are progressing quite quickly on three deals: Hugo Larsson (Frankfurt), Manuel Angel (Real Madrid) and David Affengruber (Elche).

Chelsea have agreed a £125m package to sell Enzo Fernández to Manchester City so the saga is finally coming to a close.

Chelsea will be happy with a fee that equals the British transfer record and City head coach Enzo Maresca will be delighted to land his top target.

It feels like a win-win all round as Fernández wanted to leave Chelsea and the club wanted over £120m after their initial deadline to do a deal expired.

It remains to be seen if Chelsea land any of their three main deadline day targets with a few hours of the window to go.

Chelsea had a bid rejected for Lamine Camara, Roma have not been playing ball on Manu Kone and the identity of the mystery Premier League target has not yet emerged.

Newcastle insist the only deals they are working on for the rest of the day are the departures of Nick Woltemade on loan to Juventus and Sean Neave to Wolverhampton Wanderers.

It is understood Sunderland have made contact with Benfica this afternoon to discuss terms for Lukébakio, who is another Belgium international.

Crystal Palace are believed to have offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to Fofana which could be enough to swing things in their favour.

Manchester United are in discussions about signing the 18-year-old Leicester midfielder Louis Page. Talks ongoing with Leicester but there are no guarantees a deal will happen at this stage.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets back in the spring Matías Fernández-Pardo featured prominently.

There was excitement about what he could bring to the team. There was a buzz of possibility. The 21-year-old forward had impressed everyone, from scouts to decision makers. The call to make him one of their first-choice targets, alongside Switzerland international Johan Manzambi, was unanimous. Just as it had been when Newcastle identified Alexander Isak as their leading target back in the summer of 2022.

These meetings are a place for ideas to be shared and different targets pushed. Everyone had their own opinion and various favourites, but Fernández-Pardo was, in the words of one member of Newcastle’s recruitment taskforce “the one”.

Telegraph Sport understands that Chelsea have already rejected one proposal from City for Fernández during club-to-club talks and are demanding a fee and payment terms that are favourable to them.

Chelsea also have three separate targets of their own as potential deadline signings – Lamine Camara, Manu Kone and one mystery target from the Premier League.

Monaco have already rejected a £38.5m bid from Chelsea for Camara. Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini wants to keep Kone, although negotiations continue. And there is a third target from the Premier League, who is not believed to be Morgan Gibbs-White.

Chelsea must make significant progress on one of their targets before they will sanction Fernández’s sale – and City must make another bid that is more favourable to the club.

Monaco have rejected an opening €45m bid from Chelsea for midfielder Lamine Camara. It now remains to be seen if the club increase that offer.

Sunderland have been trying to sign a winger all summer and it appears that they have finally got their man in Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

Arsenal had been linked with a move for the 21-year old Belgium international.

Of Koné, former France manager Didier Deschamps said: “He’s very effective at winning the ball back, but he shouldn’t be limited to that role of defensive midfielder, because he also makes a difference in his use of the ball.”

Austria centre-back David Affengruber has emerged as potential deadline-day deal for Fulham as they look to bolster Alvaro Arbeloa’s defence.

The Elche player has been in La Liga for two years playing regularly and fits the data model at Craven Cottage.

Fulham are also trying deals for Real Madrid’s Manuel Angel and Eintracht Frankfurt’s Hugo Larsson as midfield options.

Sunderland are expected to complete the signing of centre-back Kevin Danso from Tottenham Hotspur with the player travelling to Wearside last night for the first part of his medical.

The Austria international will initially join on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent for £25m next year.

Danso had made it clear he wanted to leave Tottenham this summer in search of regular first-team football.

Eintracht Frankfurt are in talks with Nottingham Forest over another loan move for forward Arnaud Kalimuendo.

Frankfurt signed the Frenchman on loan in January and are negotiating a return for Forest’s £26m signing from Rennes.

Oliver Glasner, Forest’s head coach, had been intent on keeping Kalimuendo but it is understood Frankfurt’s strong interest has altered the club’s thinking.

Morato, the centre-back, is expected to join West Ham United on loan.

Forest are exploring potential signings but are determined to stay calm and only pursue deals that make financial sense. A winger and a No 6 are the two priority targets if there are deals to be done.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

“If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”

It will be good news for Arsenal if Folarin Balogun completes his £40m move to Everton today. When Arsenal sold Balogun to Monaco in 2023, they negotiated a sell-on clause of 17.5 per cent. According to my maths, that means Arsenal will get £7m from this transfer. Not to be sniffed at!

Hull City are close to agreeing a fee of around £7.5m for Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas.

The Wales international has been a long-term target for Hull and negotiations are now approaching a conclusion.

Thomas has been pushing a move through and is expected to leave Stoke after one full season.

As has become the norm this summer Acun Ilicali has posted a cryptic message on X, which has prompted speculation among Hull City fans. The club has been linked with Everton holding midfielder Tim Iroegbunam.

What a couple of weeks it has been for Robert Sanchez. He came into this season as Chelsea’s No 1, but after a difficult start to the campaign and Emi Martinez’s arrival, reports suggest he could be moving away from Stamford Bridge on loan. Cesc Fabregas’s Como appears the probable destination.

Trevoh Chalobah, who left Chelsea for Como last month, has taken to his “secondary” Instagram account to post the following picture...

Meanwhile, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, striker flop Nick Woltemade is moving to Juventus on a season-long loan. The club’s record signing from as year ago at £64m is moving to Turin for a £3.5m loan fee with the Serie A squad covering the full cost of his wages.

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

Very unlikely that Liverpool will be doing any major incoming business but there may yet be some departures. Danns, a promising striker, has had injury issues and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Fax machines are whirring as the clock continues to tick towards the transfer deadline, but who does your club need to sign? Let us know in the comments below!

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1904. GdS: ‘Modric of the defence’ – Milan’s chances of landing van Dijk next summer increase

AC Milan have been incredibly interested in a move for Virgil van Dijk in recent years and the opportunity to do so may now have arrived.

Last summer, Gerry Cardinale hoped to sign van Dijk, with just a year left on his deal. However, the timing was not right and the American couldn’t make it work. Yet, that wasn’t the end of the interest and things could heat up in the early stages of next year.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Gazzetta dello Sport wrote this morning (seen below), it’s not the first opening that the Rossoneri have had with van Dijk, but it’s perhaps their biggest yet. For the first time, he’s cast doubt on his Liverpool future, with his current deal set to expire at the end of the season.

Speaking yesterday, he admitted that it would be ‘fine’ if there was a renewal offer made, but if not, he had no issue heading elsewhere.

Cardinale has been obsessed with the idea of adding the imposing Dutchman to his Diavolo defence for some time now, even trying to sign him in the summer. However, the terms of a deal weren’t right then.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t shown a strong determination to tie van Dijk down to a new deal, so the Dutchman would be free to discuss a new home in the early parts of 2027.

Milan wouldn’t be alone in their interest in a move, though. Interest from Turkey – Galatasaray, Fenerbahce and Trabzonspor – is present, as are Saudi Arabian clubs. So, it will be dependent on whether the Dutchman prioritises money or his childhood passion.

He fell in love watching Alessandro Nesta and Paolo Maldini, and now the time may come to emulate them as long as the foundations are right. So, the Rossoneri must return to the Champions League, as well as adding some other key players.

Nevertheless, his arrival would be compared to Luka Modric in defence, an elite player whose reputation is among the best of his peers. He could be the core part of a new defence for the Diavolo.

#1903. Jurgen Klopp gushing in praise for Arsenal star: ‘He is a complete package’

Jurgen Klopp has talked up Arsenal’s Kai Havertz as ‘a complete package as a top player’ as he hopes the forward can have a big impact for Germany.

The 27-year-old has won 64 caps for his country, scoring 25 goals, and was in action as Germany beat Serbia 3-1 on Friday.

The former Chelsea man will be in the team on Monday night for the crucial Nations League clash with Netherlands, as Klopp looks to take his side into the quarter-finals.

The Germany boss has looked to build confidence in Havertz by talking up the forward’s qualities, which he feels can match up to almost anyone in the game.

‘I have often faced teams defended by Kai, and I know very well in tactical preparations that facing Kai is not an easy task. He is a complete package as a top player,’ said Klopp.

‘Mikel Arteta relies heavily on him because Kai is always reliable to put in an extraordinary performance thanks to his technical capacity and intelligence.’

He added: ‘Kai and I have agreed that there is still huge potential that we want to develop further together in the national team.’

Havertz has not been in good goal-scoring form of late, netting just once in his last 13 appearances for club and country.

That was a crucial goal in a 1-0 Arsenal win over Liverpool, but finding the back of the net has not come easily for the Gunners star.

#1902. Pocognoli fears Scottish Premiership 'identity crisis' over lack of homegrown stars

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 17:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 17:55 EST, 11 November 2026

Sebastien Pocognoli believes the Premiership has an identity crisis caused by a lack of Scottish players pulling on the jersey at our top clubs.

Just six of the 26 players the newly appointed national team manager initially selected for the Nations League double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland play their football in this country’s top division.

And while the Belgian understands the attraction and the benefits of top talents moving to some of Europe’s top leagues, he’s concerned that the division which should be his first port of call when it comes to making selections is now a barren land.

‘The Scottish league misses Scottish players in the biggest teams,’ he said.

‘The league is intense and competitive, but I am not looking at this. I am looking at who is performing at the big clubs.

‘I believe that’s the most close to international level. And for that you need to play Champions League, Europa League, Conference League in some stage of the competition.

‘That is what I’m looking at. I hope that players who are performing well, let’s say in the bottom (half), can bounce to the next step to a top club inside the country.

Pocognoli has been alarmed by the lack of Scottish talent in the SPFL Premiership

Pocognoli has been impressed by the progress of young Celtic full-back Colby Donovan

‘That will make the competition more competitive, maybe you will go through after the winter into the Champions League or Europa League.

‘That gives the experience to the young Scottish players and in the end, we’d get the benefit.

‘That’s what I’m looking at more in Scottish football rather than the clubs and the style of play of clubs, that kind of thing.

‘It’s not easy because if you look at the Scottish competition, there’s not many young lads who are getting an opportunity to shine compared to Belgium, France, Germany.’

The specific issue of a lack of opportunities being afforded to players who are eligible for the Scotland under 21 side was highlighted at the recent summit at St Andrews which all 42 clubs attended.

With Turkey the only nation which currently gives fewer minutes, the SFA’s chief football officer Craig Mulholland has tabled two proposals which would see clubs obliged to offer more chances to emerging talents in both league and cup matches.

Optimistic that such changes to the rules would lead to a brighter picture further down the line, Pocognoli added: ‘Hopefully, we can see the benefits in future.

‘I follow all of the young lads, not only from the Premiership in Scotland, but also the Championship and League One because some of them are on loan.

‘My job is not only to win the next game, it’s also to prepare for what’s coming next season.

‘In one year, a lot can change. I try to support all the decisions of the clubs in Scotland regarding the fact they play Scottish players and young ones especially.

‘Colby Donovan is a good example, he played some good games for Celtic and I tried to help to accelerate his progress, then he signed a new contract and plays week after week.

‘He is not selected this time, but I think we will get the benefit later on.

‘For Findlay Curtis it’s the same, he’s not playing a lot at Rangers but I believe in his quality.

‘We need to support those type of players because we need them, but hopefully it can help his pathway at Rangers to get some minutes.

‘I hope some other players will be on the same pathway this season.’

#1901. Mauricio Pochettino plotting Man Utd reunion with USMNT favourite who has already flopped in England

By Lewis Blain | 16 Nov 2026 07:31

Manchester United could target Juventus midfielder Weston McKennie as new boss Mauricio Pochettino looks to strengthen his options at Old Trafford.

The American international has worked under Pochettino with the USMNT, and the Argentine is understood to be a major admirer of his versatility.

However, McKennie's previous spell in English football raises questions over whether he would represent the right addition for United in January.

According to reports in Italy, Pochettino could attempt to reunite with McKennie once he officially takes the reins at United.

The outgoing United States head coach has previously spoken highly of the Juventus midfielder, once describing him as the equivalent of 'McKennie plus 10' when discussing his importance to the team.

McKennie has also impressed at club level, becoming an important figure under Luciano Spalletti and making 241 appearances for Juventus.

The 28-year-old recently signed a contract extension until 2030, meaning Juventus are in a strong negotiating position and would reportedly demand a substantial offer before considering his departure.

However, the Italian club are not ruling out potential sales as they look to reshape their squad and remain within UEFA's financial regulations.

McKennie's tactical flexibility is understood to appeal to Pochettino, with the USMNT star capable of operating in several midfield roles and further forward.

A January move is therefore a possibility worth monitoring, particularly given United's need to strengthen their options in the middle of the park.

There are reasons to question whether McKennie would be the right signing for United, though, given his previous experience in the Premier League.

His loan spell at Leeds United in 2023 was largely disappointing, with the 28-year-old midfielder unable to make the desired impact as the club suffered relegation.

He made 19 appearances, collecting seven bookings, while struggling to adapt to the demands of English football and facing criticism over his fitness and discipline.

Although Leeds' wider problems contributed to their disappointing campaign, McKennie did little to establish himself as a standout performer.

His versatility and familiarity with Pochettino could make him useful, but United should arguably be targeting a higher calibre of midfielder if they want to address their long-standing problems.

With significant investment needed elsewhere in the squad, spending heavily on a player who has already struggled in England would represent a considerable gamble.

‘I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time. I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation.

#1899. Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman smashes Jude Bellingham England Under-21 record

Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman has broken two England Under-21 records previously held by Jude Bellingham in a matter of days.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player ever to play for the Three Lions at Under-21 level when he came off the bench on Friday in a 1-0 defeat to Portugal.

Dowman then started against France at Aston Gate on Monday night, scoring a dramatic late winner in a 3-2 victory.

His appearance against Portugal broke Bellingham’s record as youngest England Under-21 player and his goal against France broke the Real Madrid superstar’s record as youngest to score at this level.

Dowman was 16 years and 320 days when he scored in Bristol on Monday, while Bellingham was 17 years and 67 days old when he made his debut against Kosovo in 2020, scoring on his first appearance for England Under-21s.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Also on the scoresheet for England in the friendly win over France were Tottenham’s Mikey Moore and Manchester City’s Divin Mubama, who is on loan at Southampton this season.

Manchester City’s Rico Lewis captained Lee Carsley’s side, while the likes of Brighton’s Jack Hinshelwood and Liverpool’s Trey Nyoni were also in the starting XI.

It was Dowman who was making yet more history, though, having already become the youngest player to score in the Premier League and to make an appearance in the Champions League.

When Arsenal won the title last season, he also became the youngest player to lift the Premier League trophy.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The incredible talent does not turn 17 until December 31 and will hope to get more run outs for Arsenal before then, although he has only had one very brief substitute appearance for the Gunners since his red card against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on October 27.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was clearly fuming with Dowman when he was shown a straight red card for reacting to a heavy challenge against Fleetwood, giving the youngster stern words as he left the field.

Arteta said: ‘I haven’t seen the reaction to my reaction, whether it is positive or negative. But you need to understand the context and the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

‘But, I don’t know. You can have another reaction. If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me some days you might say “I don’t like the reaction”. For me, it was the best reaction to be who I am.’

He added: ‘The reaction when I don’t win, you want to know what my reaction is? I am [angry] big time.

‘So, we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality, otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League and this level.

‘We look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time we are going to demand from him, like everybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Because the other boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair.’

By Lewis Blain | 16 Nov 2026 07:53, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 07:53

Liverpool and Chelsea are among three Premier League clubs monitoring AC Milan defender Koni De Winter ahead of the January transfer window.

The 24-year-old has impressed at the San Siro this season, attracting attention alongside Manchester United.

However, the Serie A giants are reluctant to sanction his departure and consider him an important part of their long-term defensive plans.

According to reports in Italy (via Sport Witness), Liverpool, Chelsea and United have all 'shown interest' in De Winter after his impressive start to the 2026-27 campaign.

The Belgium international joined Milan from Genoa in the summer of 2025 and made 26 appearances in his debut season, gradually establishing himself as a reliable defensive option.

He has taken another step forward this term, featuring 11 times in Serie A and becoming an important member of the backline under ex-Red Devils boss Ruben Amorim.

De Winter's versatility is particularly attractive, having demonstrated an ability to operate in both a back three and a conventional back four.

His physical attributes and composure in possession have also helped him develop into an increasingly complete defender, with Milan viewing the £20m-rated titan as a potential future leader.

The Rossoneri are keen to strengthen their own defence in January, with Sporting CP's Goncalo Inacio reportedly a major target, but that does not necessarily mean De Winter will be allowed to leave.

Liverpool and Chelsea could find themselves competing for several of the same players in January, with both clubs looking to strengthen their defensive options and improve the overall balance of their squads.

Their joint interest in AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is another example, with both Premier League sides having been linked with a £100m move for the highly-rated Englishman.

De Winter would offer a different type of opportunity, potentially providing either club with a versatile defensive option capable of covering multiple positions.

There are clear similarities between the recruitment needs of the Reds and the Blues, meaning their paths could cross repeatedly as the winter window approaches.

However, Milan's determination to retain De Winter means a deal will not be straightforward, particularly if they are unwilling to entertain anything short of a substantial offer.

With Scott and De Winter both on their respective radars, the two English clubs could be set for an intriguing January transfer battle.
