Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

When Rice missed the last international break, in came Alex Scott to partner Anderson and the balance produced helped to deliver a blistering 7-0 win in Rijeka, Croatia’s heaviest-ever defeat.

Back in came Rice this month and he and Anderson complemented each other superbly as all-action anchors in Madrid until Anderson’s sending off and England’s 10-man survival job. Up to the red card, England’s pass completion rate was better than Spain’s — almost unheard of.

England have embraced the Premier League and modern club football over the past eight years or so in order to become far more like a club team themselves, and the way Tuchel’s team is evolving just so happens to introduce a couple of club link-ups that are already improving on-field chemistry.

On the left, Lewis Hall of Newcastle United is making the left-back position his own. And further forward he can interchange with a player he knows very well indeed. Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon stepped up his game in an England shirt in 2026 and earned his move to Catalonia following three and a half years at Newcastle. It is clear they know each other’s games inside out.

The opposite flank has the potential to become all about Arsenal. Ben White scored England’s third against Spain and is well-placed to nail down the right-back position in 2027. Alongside him in England’s strongest XI would be the Three Lions’ best centre-back, Ezri Konsa, and in midfield, Rice. On the right wing, once back fit: Bukayo Saka. An Arsenal quartet playing with each other week in, week out would only help England’s coherence on the pitch.

Here is a factor not to be underestimated. Spain, Portugal and France will all join England among the eight quarter-finalists in March, but they have all won trophies in recent years.

England have been just about the most consistent team in international football not just in Europe but right across the world since Gareth Southgate’s team reached the 2018 World Cup semi-finals, and yet a succession of quite or very near misses has still left them without silverware. The years of hurt continue as winning the World Cup in 1966 becomes an ever-more distant memory.

It is the common view, though, that the greatest period in England’s men’s history is the one we are currently in, and a trophy of some sort at some point does feel an inevitability.

Bellingham, Kane and Tuchel all possess the self-confidence and courage England need to finally conquer that final mountain. Gordon and Rice share the same winning mentality. England are one of the very best teams in the world and have nothing to fear. And, crucially, they may want it just that little bit more.

#1864. Mary Fowler was offered a record $1million to return home and reunite with Nathan Cleary - but she said no

Published: 21:52 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 21:57 EST, 11 November 2026

A reported record-breaking pay offer and the chance to live closer to Nathan Cleary were not enough to bring Mary Fowler back to Australia.

The Matildas star remains at Manchester City after a reported $1million offer emerged as part of an ambitious plan to recruit Australian sport’s glamour couple to two clubs under the same ownership umbrella.

The proposal could have offered a solution to the long-distance relationship that keeps their careers on opposite sides of the world.

For battling NRL franchise Wests Tigers, it was an extraordinary bid to prise one of rugby league’s biggest names away from Penrith.

According to News Corp, Tigers owner Holman Barnes Group proposed a combined package worth $9million, including a $1million marquee contract for Fowler to join the Central Coast Mariners women’s team.

The group had acquired the Mariners women’s side, opening the door to a recruitment pitch spanning two sports.

Mary Fowler remains at Manchester City despite a reported $1million offer to return to Australian football

A proposed recruitment package would have brought Fowler to the Central Coast Mariners and Cleary to Wests Tigers

Fowler returned to Australia in October to support Cleary following two operations

Under the reported proposal, Cleary would have joined the Tigers and Fowler would have returned to NSW on what would be the highest salary in A-League Women history.

But the blockbuster homecoming did not materialise.

Fowler, 23, is contracted to Manchester City until 2028, meaning any move would also require an agreement with the English club over her release.

She has built a formidable profile away from the pitch, with News Corp reporting that her multi-year Adidas deal is worth $10million.

Her other commercial work includes a L’Oréal Paris ambassadorship and Chobani’s national ‘Game Changer’ campaign.

The couple’s long-distance relationship attracted renewed attention in October when Fowler returned to Australia to support Cleary as he recovered from two operations.

She withdrew from Matildas friendlies against Germany and Haiti for personal reasons in October, prompting questions about her sudden absence.

Football Australia said the decision followed discussions between Fowler, Manchester City and Matildas staff.

Fowler’s commercial pulling power extends well beyond football, with  her multi-year Adidas deal worth $10million

Fowler became L’Oréal Paris’s first female athlete ambassador for Australia and New Zealand in 2024, adding a major beauty partnership to her growing profile

Fowler fronts Chobani’s national ‘Game Changer’ campaign, appearing across billboards, public transport and digital advertising as the brand launches its high-protein drinks

Should athletes choose love or loyalty to their teams when faced with life-changing offers?

Teammate Hayley Raso revealed the news had caught her by surprise.

‘I haven’t spoken to Mary. I only just found out the news myself,’ Raso said.

‘Obviously, Mary’s a really valuable player for our team, so it’s sad that she’s not here at this camp, but obviously, she has to take care of some personal circumstances.’

Cleary had fractured his fibula and dislocated his ankle during Penrith’s preliminary final loss to Newcastle, with a bone breaking through the skin.

He also had a fracture in his other foot.

Panthers chairman Greg Alexander later explained that the damage, while confronting, could have been worse.

‘The tibia didn’t break, no fracture in the tibia, which was fantastic news,’ Alexander told SEN.

‘In terms of the horrific injury that Nathan suffered, it was as good as could be expected without the double fracture.’

Cleary has since reportedly passed up another offer to remain with the club where he won four consecutive premierships.

The NRL expansion club the PNG Chiefs proposed a package worth up to $8.4million over three years, according to News Corp.

That reportedly included $6million in tax-free playing payments and a potential $2.4million in third-party endorsements.

Nine reported that Cleary told the Chiefs he intended to stay at Penrith, where he was expected to sign a two-year extension through to the end of 2029.

#1861. Who is Silvia Tuya? New Manchester United female coach set to make history

Manchester United are set to make history with the appointment of Silvia Tuya as part of Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom staff.

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal revive Vinicius talks; Man Utd want Hall

Arsenal’s next two deals revealed after major contract breakthrough

Mauricio Pochettino urged to make Chelsea star first Man Utd signing

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Man Utd have already agreed a £9m compensation package with the US Soccer Federation to extract Pochettino from his contract as manager of the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT).

Following the Argentine to Old Trafford will be long-serving lieutenants, including assistant manager Jesus Perez and goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez.

But Pochettino will also bring newer additions to his coaching team, including strength and conditioning coach Tuya in what will be a first for Man United.

Silvia Tuya - full name Silvia Tuya Vinas - is a strength and conditioning coach, currently employed by the USMNT.

Tuya will become the first female coach of the men’s first team squad at Old Trafford, creating history ahead of a new chapter for Manchester United.

The strength and conditioning coach will be familiar with creating such history, having previously become the first female coach in the history of the USMNT’s senior squad when she joined the backroom staff in October 2024.

Tuya holds a doctorate of science in high performance and is fluent in English, Spanish, and Catalan.

She has previously lectured at the University of Barcelona and National Institute of Physical Education of Catalonia, before joining Pochettino’s USA set up in October 2024.

Prior to the move to the States, the Spaniard briefly worked with FC Badalona in her native Catalonia, the team competing in Liga F - the top-flight of the women’s game in Spain.

Tuya also worked with Levante’s women's team, and has experience in strength and conditioning athletes from other disciplines, such as tennis, rugby, basketball, and ironman competitors.

The specialist in strength and conditioning was in charge of physical preparation at Levante, and will likely work closely with fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino - son of Mauricio - at Man United.

A PhD fellow, Tuya has contributed to different scientific papers, including research into reactions in football.

While certain members of Pochettino’s backroom staff have already travelled to England, the Guardian claim Tuya, analyst Alec Scott and Miguel D’Agostino have remained with the USA camp ahead of the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final second leg with Haiti.

As such, Tuya will be expected to start work at Carrington from November 18 - the same day as Pochettino.

Man United agreed that Pochettino could take charge of the USA’s games against Haiti before starting work at Carrington and Old Trafford.

#1860. Cardinale discusses MSE creation and evolution within Milan: “Helping write a new chapter”

With the news of the new company leading AC Milan, Gerry Cardinale has offered a few words about what it means for the project.

In recent minutes, RedBird have announced a new parent company for Milan, aptly named ‘Milan Sports & Entertainment’. It’s a project that aims to put all of the club’s investments under one umbrella, whilst also allowing further investment into the city.

The new stadium is believed to have played a big part in this decision, and the Rossoneri will hopefully benefit significantly from this move.

As MilanNews relays, Cardinale offered some words in the announcement about the creation of the company, what it means to the city and for Rossoneri fans, what it means for the club.

“Over the past 25 years, we have worked alongside rights holders in the sports and media sectors to create innovative businesses that have transformed their respective industries.

“This evolution is based on a deep respect for the intellectual property assets that underpin these businesses, a long-term partnership with rights holders, and the ambition to fully unlock the potential of these teams and leagues, both on and off the pitch.

“Milan Sports & Entertainment represents the culmination of this journey and the work we have carried out since we first invested in AC Milan four years ago. Becoming a club owner has given us an even deeper understanding of what creates long-term value: winning, serving fans, and investing in the communities that give these institutions meaning.

“Today, we apply this experience on a different scale: not just to a single club, a single sport, or a single facility, but to an entire city and a portfolio that spans sports, lifestyle, and entertainment. I have known Brett Yormark and worked with him for 25 years.

“We’ve been working with Milan for years, and I can’t imagine a better executive in the international sports industry to help execute this strategy. Thanks to Brett, we can bring the best of American sports and live entertainment to Milan, helping write a new chapter in the city’s growth and international success.

“With AC Milan as our cornerstone, which will always be the driving force behind all our initiatives, we intend to build a world-class sports and entertainment platform capable of shaping the future of Milan and European sports, and bringing it back to the forefront of the global stage.”

Considering how much attention Cardinale has paid to the future of the Diavolo, and taking them back to the top level, it’s nice to hear it referenced once again in his latest statement. Hopefully this move is another step towards that.

#1858. Tottenham starting to carve out new identity under Roberto De Zerbi as rest of season predicted

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

After a tricky start to the season, Tottenham have begun to find their feet under Roberto De Zerbi.

Despite spending more than £300million on new players over the summer, Spurs were bottom of the Premier League table before the September international break.

They have since found form, though, losing just one of their next five games and, after an unbeaten October, De Zerbi was crowned Premier League Manager of the Month last week.

Spurs endured a nightmare opening weekend as their expensively assembled squad was dismantled 3-0 by Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Performances have since improved, though, and Spurs produced a result for the ages when they beat Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge to secure just their second win in 42 attempts at the Blues’ home ground.

Defeat to Leeds in their last game was a setback, but overall performances have steadily evolved, and Spurs are starting to carve out an identity under De Zerbi.

Spurs embarked on a comprehensive squad overhaul during the summer as they parted ways with a number of senior players while also looking to build a team in De Zerbi’s image.

The addition of centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke, who worked under De Zerbi at Brighton, has proven an astute piece of business, and he has begun to develop a solid partnership with fellow Dutch international Micky van de Ven.

In midfield, Spurs went big, splashing £185m on Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali. The pair have taken a bit of time to acclimatise, but recently they have begun to develop an understanding with each other.

There is still a lot more to come, though, from Spurs’ attacking signings, with Savio and Mykhailo Mudryk struggling for fitness while striker Omar Marmoush has flattered to deceive since arriving from Manchester City.

Having guided Spurs to Premier League survival last season, De Zerbi has plenty of goodwill in the bank, and it is why his job didn’t come under serious scrutiny when Spurs failed to win any of their first five league games.

The Italian’s substitutions have drawn criticism, and Spurs still struggle to react to going behind, but overall De Zerbi has his team playing with intensity and personality.

Issues still persist in attack, but that is as much down to personnel as it is De Zerbi’s tactics. Either way, though, he will have to find a way to make Spurs more efficient in the final third.

#1856. Newcastle’s limitations exposed by Bournemouth before hosts fight back for draw

This was the definition of a hard-earned point. Newcastle United came back from two goals down to rescue a point against Bournemouth, but this was not a convincing performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side.

Newcastle were abject for the first half an hour and the visitors could have been out of sight. It was disjointed and lacklustre as Bournemouth dominated before the break and regularly threatened Lukasz Hornicek in goal.

Even during the fightback, Newcastle lacked cohesion and penetration, but forced their way back into it through hard work, spirit and determination. Whether you believe Harvey Barnes’ wonder goal and Jacob Ramsey’s late strike paper over the cracks or reveal a togetherness – a grit and determination that bodes well for the future – depends on the individual.

Ramsey comes off the bench to fire Newcastle level! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UBWAfCQyy4

For the second weekend in a row, Newcastle had just two shots on target and scored two goals. At the other end of the pitch, they have allowed their opponents 61 shots in just three games, the highest in the division. That is not going to be sustainable long term. Something Jaissle acknowledged.

“It shows where we have potential,” he said. “There are elements to improve offensively.

“The learning curve is there. There were some elements missing from our performance but there was a strong response. The lads showed big character, big personality and big commitment... It is always better to get a point and see the potential to improve.”

A reality check is not necessarily a bad thing. There has been a lot of hype and excitement on Tyneside and a self-congratulating tone to their own end of summer appraisals.

But this was a reminder of the team’s limitations and the fact that only three of their eight summer signings started the game, with two more coming off the bench, underlined they are a work in progress.

In truth, that is fine. It is the start of September and the Premier League campaign is only three games old. They have a new manager and a new-look team. There has been a significant amount of change in a very short period of time.

It was not the easiest summer, and despite the insistence from senior figures at the club that they had always remained calm and methodical during their summer reset, there was a whiff of crisis only a few weeks ago.

When Eddie Howe quit as manager and Bruno Guimarães, the captain, forced his move to Arsenal at the start of August, Newcastle looked in disarray. So, to have started the season unbeaten from three games against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth is encouraging.

It is also worth highlighting just how good the visitors were. In the first half Bournemouth were superb, rushing Newcastle, forcing mistakes and pouring forward in numbers. In Alex Scott, just as he was in their victory here last season, Bournemouth had the best player on the pitch.

That opens up another conversation. Newcastle played like this a lot at home in Howe’s final season in charge, especially in the second-half of the campaign, but tended to lose not draw the game.

On this occasion, they secured a decent point with a late equaliser thanks to substitute Ramsey, who looked good when he replaced the off-colour Lewis Miley.

Bournemouth will feel they should have held on. They had taken a deserved lead through Marcus Tavernier, who took advantage of a static and ball-watching Amar Dedić to bundle home from close range.

Tavernier gives Bournemouth the lead at St James' Park! 🍒🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/mDdb5uV4hj

Marco Rose’s side should have scored again minutes later when Sven Botman gifted the ball to Evanilson on the edge of the Newcastle area, but he failed to hit the target.

Bournemouth had their tails up and when another blunder from Dedic – galloping forward and losing possession with a heavy touch – Nico González, another new signing, failed to make a tackle to stop the attack.

Justin Kluivert’s long-range strike thumped against the post and hit the back of goalkeeper Lukasz Hornicek. Scott reacted quickest and his cross spun into his own net off the leg of Malick Thiaw.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Newcastle were in disarray and were lucky to be back in the game before half-time as Barnes whipped in a stunning strike 25 seconds after the restart.

Bournemouth have a second and St James' Park is stunned! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Kyy91awf39

Despite seeing more of the ball, other than a Joe Willock header that dropped wide of the post early in the second half, Newcastle did not create another clear goal-scoring opportunity until Ramsey’s equaliser.

That is a cause for concern, but Newcastle remain unbeaten. Nothing shapes perceptions more than results. Jaissle is right to cling to the positives from that.

Speaking to TNT Sports, the Newcastle boss said: “Mixed feelings. Happy for that spirit, that belief the lads were showing until the end together with the crowd. I felt the energy and felt if we had five or 10 minutes more we could win this game. But the first half was not expected. This is something we need to improve. This is part of the journey.

“We knew Bournemouth would come with everything, they always show great intensity and if you do not compete with that you get problems. We struggled with that in the first half but the lads showed the right reaction.”

"I'm really happy with the confidence the lads brought onto the pitch today." 👏Marco Rose reflects on Bournemouth's performance after taking a point at St James' Park.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GULqEAUSbx

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday lunchtime fixture between Newcastle United and Bournemouth at St James’ Park.

The hosts have made a determined start to the 2025-26 season under new head coach Matthias Jaissle. They conceded a last-minute penalty to draw 2-2 with Liverpool on the opening weekend of the Premier League campaign, sealed a hard-fought 3-2 victory over West Bromwich Albion in the Carabao Cup, and then produced an inspired second-half performance to win 2-0 away at Tottenham in their previous top-flight outing.

Despite anxiety in the summer after losing Eddie Howe and multiple key players such as Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon, the Jaissle era has begun very encouragingly. New signings including Lukas Hornicek, Amar Dedic and Nico Gonzalez have seamlessly slotted into the starting XI, Lewis Hall has been typically brilliant, while Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa look reborn up top after both forwards endured difficult campaigns last season.

Marco Rose’s Bournemouth tenure has started in frustrating circumstances. They had been leading 1-0 against Manchester City in their first top-flight fixture this campaign, but conceded two late goals to dramatically lose 2-1. Bournemouth were also left kicking themselves last weekend against Everton, after a defensive mix-up between Ryan Christie and Marcus Tavernier following a corner delivery gifted James Tarkowski a 91st-minute equaliser, allowing the visitors to salvage a 1-1 draw at the Vitality Stadium.

At opposite ends of the country, over 350 miles separate these two sides. Away days in English football can’t really get any longer. The travelling Bournemouth support will hope their loyalty can be repaid with a first Premier League win of the season under Rose, while Newcastle will aim to continue their unbeaten start and carry on the positive momentum created by Jaissle.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1855. Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku announces shock retirement from international football

By Darren Plant | 16 Nov 2026 11:05

Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku has announced that he has retired from international football.

With 94 goals from 135 appearances, the Fenerbahce striker is Belgium's all-time record goalscorer.

Lukaku's most recent outing for Belgium was against France on November 5, the 33-year-old donning the captain's armband on that occasion.

However, Lukaku did not play in Belgium's last two fixtures, being ruled out versus Turkey last Thursday due to a hip injury and remaining as an unused substitute for Sunday's 4-1 victory over Italy.

On Monday morning, Lukaku took to social media to make the surprise revelation that he had called time on his international career.

A statement on Instagram read: "Over these 16 years, I gave everything for the national team…I experienced every emotion imaginable…

"I was lucky enough to play alongside extraordinary teammates, to whom I will always be grateful. I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches who pushed me to give my best and trusted me to help the team. It was a wonderful journey, and I cherished every moment.

"To the Belgian fans, thank you for all the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships.

"I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was incredible. I enjoyed it immensely. I am grateful. Thank you."

Under both Rudi Garcia at the World Cup and Mark van Bommel across the six recent UEFA Nations League matches, Lukaku has not been viewed as a certain starter.

That is despite the former Chelsea, Everton and Manchester United forward scoring in four of his last seven outings for his country.

While Lukaku has not shed light on any potential issues behind the scenes, an assumption can be made that remaining as an unused substitute in two of the five games that he was available under Van Bommel has played its part.

At the age of 33, Lukaku had the opportunity to join a list of players who have reached 100 goals for their country. Only Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Ali Daei have achieved that feat.

Choosing to stay six goals short of the illustrious three figures feels an unusual choice on Lukaku's part, but it does not take away from ending his international career with 53 goals more than any other Belgian player in history.

#1853. How Michael Carrick's Man United fell apart: Players' bust-up on flight back from Madrid, weakness in training and on touchline - and why dressing-room sources believe divided board 'hung him out to dry'

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 10:30 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:44 EST, 12 November 2026

For the last two days, Michael Carrick has followed his familiar route towards Manchester United’s training base, nudging his black Land Rover past the security barrier at Carrington before 8am, and making his way into work just as he has for much of the last two decades as a player, coach and head coach at the club.

While Carrick's fate has been decided by men in suits in Monaco and Manchester, he has put on his training gear and gone through the motions of coaching whichever players are left during the international break.

It has become increasingly apparent that Carrick was a dead man walking in the two weeks since the United board gave him a stay of execution and bought themselves time after the 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth last month.

Having effectively been brought in as a caretaker when United plucked him off the beach in Barbados in mid-January, he left much the same way: merely keeping the seat warm for Mauricio Pochettino in the chaotic days that have led to his sacking.

Sources close to the United dressing room believe Carrick has been ‘hung out to dry’ as United dithered over his future and then began a futile attempt to appoint Pochettino as his replacement in secret.

This is the story of how Carrick's United fell apart. It is the story of how disgruntled players aired their dirty laundry in public and clashed in private. It is the story of how the club's boardroom became the backdrop for an executive power struggle. And it is the story of how the magic touch that saw Carrick land the job permanently just five months ago deserted him...

Michael Carrick is out as Manchester United manager - just ten league games after guiding United to third and being handed a two-year contract

Carrick has had to turn up as normal at Carrington this week even as the world knew he was for the chop. Some dressing-room sources say he has been 'hung out to dry'

Carrick would have seen the writing on the wall when he got up to give an impressive speech at a dinner in the Heritage Suite at Old Trafford on Friday night to celebrate the 40th anniversary of Sir Alex Ferguson’s appointment.

The significance of the occasion was not lost on Carrick. Ferguson was brought in to succeed Ron Atkinson on the same date in November 1986 with United one place above the relegation zone. Having boxed himself into an identical corner, Carrick too was on borrowed time.

Two days later, he stood helplessly on the touchline at Old Trafford as United played out a ridiculous 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. Twice his team fought back from two goals down, but it was the final proof for United bosses that change was unavoidable.

The biggest club in English football having to endure the humiliation of at least two weeks in the relegation zone was too much for them to stomach.

His body language after the Bournemouth game when a tearful and crestfallen Carrick offered what looked like a farewell wave to the Stretford End – four days after he approached fans in Como to apologise for an equally painful 4-1 Champions League surrender – suggested he was already done.

The 45-year-old limped on to another defeat at Chelsea, then presided over a barmy 3-2 comeback win over Roma and the bonkers draw with Villa. A consummate and composed midfielder for United, Carrick of all people knew this wasn’t the way football should be played.

All the while, he spoke like a man who could turn things around. They always do. But the performances and results told a different story.

His critics would argue that someone whose only previous job in management was at Middlesbrough should never have been put in charge of United in the first place.

Others would say the bravest move by the club would have been to thank Carrick for his admirable efforts in securing third place and Champions League qualification last season, and move on in the summer when Pochettino would have been available for free before signing a new contract as US coach with a £7million release clause.

Matheus Cunha's late winner sealed a remarkable comeback win over Roma last week - but it promised to be a false dawn for Carrick

The 45-year-old's body language after an earlier loss to Bournemouth had suggested he was done back then, with Carrick appearing to wave farewell to the Stretford End

Instead, Carrick was rewarded with a two-year deal in May and the wheels fell off in spectacular fashion. Rather like his friend and former team-mate Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the honeymoon period gave way to something altogether less appealing.

At least Solskjaer stuck around for three more years. Having beaten the Norwegian to the job in January, Carrick’s reign lasted less than 10 months.

The similarities between the two men are striking. Ex-players who basked in the glory days under Ferguson and know what it takes to succeed at Old Trafford, but were incapable of lifting the modern-day Manchester United to similar heights.

Having replaced Ruben Amorim and inspired a remarkable turnaround in the second half of last season, Carrick must have thought he had a chance.

His calm demeanour and experience of life in the Old Trafford pressure cooker that had played a part in his appointment was in contrast to the emotional incontinence of Amorim. How strange then that it has given way to such calamity and chaos.

United got off to the worst possible start by losing at newly-promoted Hull City in August. Tigers boss Sergej Jakirovic belittled them by saying his goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis might as well have been sipping a cup of tea, and the hits have just kept on coming for Carrick.

Aside from Bournemouth, there were the late equalisers scored by Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Dominic Solanke for Everton and Tottenham, the controversial winner conceded to 10-man Manchester City, crashing out of the Carabao Cup to Brighton after giving up a two-goal lead, and the defeats in Europe by Atletico Madrid and Como after going behind in the opening seconds.

By the time Alysson scored in the first minute for Villa on Sunday, United’s defence had become as leaky as the Old Trafford roof. The four goals Carrick’s side conceded took it to 15 in his final four games.

United's defence has been leaky all season long, with Ainsley Maitland-Niles' stoppage-time equaliser at Hill Dickinson Stadium among the goals to cost them valuable points

By the time Alysson scored in the first minute for Aston Villa on Sunday, United’s defence had become as leaky as the Old Trafford roof. They let in 15 in his final four games

So why the alarming decline from last season? The United players haven’t looked sharp after a disjointed World Cup summer that involved a more relaxed one-week training camp in Ireland. There have been too many injuries.

Some players have spoken of a drop-off in training under Carrick and his backroom staff. Others feel that the switch to a more possession-based 4-2-4 system was asking too much of a group who aren’t suited to it.

There was surprise that a man so invested in the club's academy used so few young players. Harry Amass was left kicking his heels despite the chronic shortage of left backs, JJ Gabriel's shock exit was an unwelcome distraction, and Shea Lacey's re-emergence came too late.

It would be grossly unfair to pin this all on Carrick though. He is just the latest unfortunate to pay the price for the shambles at United which runs from the boardroom to the dressing room.

Amid ongoing uncertainty over his future, there has been a power struggle behind the scenes between director of football Jason Wilcox and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell over who to replace him, while sources close to the Glazer family have revealed a growing dissatisfaction at how minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos are running the club.

United failed Carrick in the transfer market last summer with a futile pursuit of his No 1 midfield target Elliot Anderson, and instead delivered Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos.

Carrick could see trouble on the horizon when he spoke to the media at Carton House in Maynooth during that pre-season camp in early August, but tried not to rock the boat.

It was the day his daughter Louise was getting her A-level results. ‘You know, we would like more, we need to keep pushing for more,’ he said, using the word ‘push’ another nine times.

There has been a power struggle behind the scenes between director of football Jason Wilcox (centre) and director of recruitment Christopher Vivell (left) over who to replace Carrick

Some players have spoken of a drop-off in training under Carrick and his backroom staff

Carlos Baleba followed but an ankle injury meant that he couldn’t play until October, and the £70m signing then suffered a hamstring injury.

United blundered catastrophically by focusing on midfield and delaying improvements to other areas of the team until next summer. In particular, the decision not to sign cover for Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko backfired spectacularly as both players succumbed to injury.

Lisandro Martinez called out United’s underwhelming recruitment in Madrid by saying he expected more of Wilcox, and he isn’t the only one who feels that way.

Tielemans gave a terse ‘no comment’ when he was asked on camera about his team-mate’s remarks, but it’s understood the two players clashed on the team flight back to Manchester as cracks began to show in an increasingly unhappy camp.

The camaraderie fostered by rounds of golf involving Carrick and the players during the break in Ireland was beginning to fall apart.

It came to a head when captain Bruno Fernandes became the second member of the leadership group to speak out of turn, questioning Carrick’s tactics after the loss to Como.

Having continuously defended his players in the face of criticism from some of his former United team-mates over their lack of effort, Carrick’s spiky response that ‘if you don't run forward and you don't run back, you aren’t going to win’ perhaps revealed his true feelings about this group.

He and Fernandes settled their differences in a clear-the-air meeting, but the questions didn’t go away. When he was asked about their relationship again at the end of what proved to be his final pre-match press conference last Friday, Carrick tapped his inquisitor on the shoulder as he left the room at Carrington and said with a smile: ‘Nice try!’

It was typical of Carrick, who often met questions with the knowing grin of a man who couldn’t say what he really thought.

Lisandro Martinez and Youri Tielemans clashed on United's flight back to Manchester following the former's incendiary comments after a loss to Atletico Madrid

One issue has been Carrick’s rather passionless appearance on the touchline. ‘He doesn't upset anyone, but doesn't inspire anyone either,’ remarked one dressing room source

It got to the point where he was encouraged by the club to be a little more forthcoming in press conferences. There have been some barbed post-match exchanges in TV interviews with Sky Sports and Viaplay this season, and the five-minute monologue before the Bournemouth game was pure theatre.

But on the whole, Carrick’s ability to play a straight bat in front of the cameras was a welcome change for the Old Trafford hierarchy compared to the loose-lipped Amorim – particularly with the Amazon Prime documentary-makers following their every move.

‘He talks a lot but doesn't say much,’ said Roy Keane, never Carrick’s biggest fan, on Sunday. ‘I don't know if that's a tactic, like a politician.’

More of an issue was Carrick’s rather passionless appearance on the touchline, which seemed to be reflected in his team at times.

Always dressed in black, a hand placed studiously on his chin, it has contrasted with more animated adversaries such as Unai Emery, Roberto De Zerbi and Diego Simeone in recent weeks.

‘He doesn't upset anyone, but doesn't inspire anyone either,’ remarked one dressing room source.

The fans were always behind him though, even the ones who may have accepted some time ago that a change was needed. Support and sympathy were never in short supply for a coach who has been let down by the men in the directors’ box and the players on the pitch.

That much has been abundantly clear by the abuse meted out to Ratcliffe and Co this season, and the unprecedented scenes when the fans turned on the players after Bournemouth.

Carrick looks set to be replaced by former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino (right)

Carrick has been known to stand alongside them in the past, and it would be no surprise to see him there again in future.

‘Oh, it’s Carrick you know…’ echoed his tribute song from the Stretford End as he disappeared down the tunnel for the last time on Sunday evening.

So another bites the dust. A good man. A United man. The right man for the job? Maybe not, as it turns out. That poisoned chalice now passes to Mauricio Pochettino.

#1850. Why Man United decided against appointing Didier Deschamps as their new head coach

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 11:52, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 11:55

Manchester United had reportedly considered Didier Deschamps as a replacement for Michael Carrick, but conversations with the Frenchman and his representatives over a move to Old Trafford 'did not go well'.

Carrick was sacked by Man United last week due to the team's struggles in the early months of the 2026-27 campaign, and Mauricio Pochettino has since been appointed at his replacement, with the Argentine due to officially take charge on November 18.

In the latter stages of Carrick's time at Old Trafford, there were suggestions that Deschamps was being seriously considered as a replacement for the Englishman.

According to The Athletic, contact was made over a potential move for the 58-year-old, who stepped down as France head coach following the 2026 World Cup.

However, the report claims that the conversations 'did not go well'.

Man United allegedly believed that Deschamps was looking to gain leverage for a move to manage in Saudi Arabia.

Deschamps has been in charge of Monaco, Juventus and Marseille during his club management career, while he was France's boss between 2012 and 2026.

The former midfielder guided Monaco to success in the Coupe de la Ligue, in addition to overseeing a spot in the 2003-04 Champions League final.

Deschamps also lifted the Serie B title in 2006-07 while in charge of Juventus, in addition to Ligue 1, three Coupe de la Ligue trophies and two Trophee des Champions while at Marseille.

For France, Deschamps guided the team to the 2018 World Cup and 2020-21 UEFA Nations League trophies, in addition to helping the Blues reach the final of Euro 2016 and 2022 World Cup.

Deschamps is thought to be in line for a move to Saudi Arabia at some stage in the near future.

Antonio Conte, Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe were also all linked with the role at Old Trafford before Pochettino's arrival was confirmed.

Pochettino will be aiming to make the perfect start to life at Man United when the Red Devils head to Liverpool in the Premier League this weekend.

#1848. De Rossi admits Genoa ‘lost well’ to Milan and recalls Moreira’s comment: “Even our opponents notice”

Daniele De Rossi has looked back at Genoa’s defeat to AC Milan and how he wasn’t frustrated with his team afterwards.

Milan entered the international break with a much-needed victory against Genoa, but it wasn’t the easiest result of the season. After a disappointing defeat to Ferencvaros – which extended the midweek run of defeats – they couldn’t afford to drop points, and they succeeded, even if it wasn’t without flaw.

With two goals inside 20 minutes, you’d be forgiven for expecting Milan to win by more than a couple. However, that was the end of their goalscoring for the afternoon and although Genoa pulled one back, they didn’t grab more than a consolation goal.

Speaking to Sky Sport – in the new series ‘Radici’ – De Rossi looked back on the defeat to the Rossoneri, as well as a comment that stuck with him from Diego Moreira, as MilanPress have relayed today.

We indeed lost against Milan, but we lost ‘well.’ We didn’t deserve it. Three or four weeks ago, the latest results seemed like a pipe dream. I thank the players, staff, and my club for giving me faith and patience at a time when other clubs wouldn’t have had it.

“They remembered how good we did last year. I’m happy to have emerged from a difficult period and to be Genoa’s coach; I’m really happy there.”

“I’m passionate about the fans and the supporters. I’m part of a club that, in terms of fan base, is among the best in Europe. I’m passionate; I don’t punch a clock. I spend two hours with the stockman or the waitress with the same enthusiasm I spend time with the team captain. Experiencing it like that, you realise that Genoa is a great team.

“Genoa is full of Genoese fans who remind you every second how much they love their club, the pride of being the top club in Italy. The architecture of the stadium and the warmth of the fans… I’m not saying this to be a sycophant, but on Sunday Moreira came to me and said, ‘I’ve never seen anything like this here in Italy.’ It’s a reality that even our opponents notice.”

#1847. Alfie Whiteman interview: Life is short, I left Tottenham and football to experience the world

From the Europa League final to the Prince Charles Cinema, the former goalkeeper is carving out a new career

Trawl through Alfie Whiteman’s most recent Instagram post, and you will stumble across a fridge cluttered with magnets, polaroid pictures and a Europa League winners medal.

There, hidden within a carousel of charity shops, cameras and cats, lies a perfectly understated summation of where football figures for a man who cut short his professional career at just 26, not through injury or mental distress, but to pursue a passion for the arts.

Whiteman spent 16 years as a goalkeeper at his boyhood club, Tottenham, but he admits he has not been back to watch them live since hanging up his gloves in October last year.

“I had an offer,” Whiteman tells Standard Sport after taking part in a live Q&A for the launch of Together Tottenham - a new shared mission between the club and Spurs in the Community to create 150,000 meaningful opportunities for local young people by 2030.

Life is short, and I wanted to make sure I experienced the other wonderful things the world has to offer

“I could have continued to play, but I think for many years prior I was always planning for life after (football).

“Life is short, and I wanted to make sure I experienced the other wonderful things the world has to offer, but it was a huge decision that came with a lot of self-doubt and risk because there wasn’t something set up for me to look into.”

Whiteman stepped into the unknown in pursuit of his “purpose beyond the sport”. But it is a decision he is grateful he took after years spent living a “double life” in which his creative instincts were “discouraged”.

Physically and metaphorically, he had closed the door on his football career, locking away his Europa League and 2019 Champions League runners-up medal in a drawer before eventually putting them pride of place alongside pictures of his friends and family.

He continued: “It’s funny. For a long time they (the medals) were just in a drawer, but I thought I’d put them out as a reminder for me of all the wonderful experiences that my life and football gave me and how hard I worked.

“My whole childhood was essentially devoted to battling my way through the footballing system, which famously is not an easy one to go through.”

Whiteman only ever made one senior competitive appearance for Spurs, coming on as an 82nd-minute substitute for Joe Hart in a 4–0 Europa League win against Ludogorets Razgrad in November 2020.

However, his connection to the club remains strong, and he admits the 2025 Europa League triumph against Manchester United, which ended Spurs’ 17-year wait for a major trophy, was the perfect send-off.

“I look back on it as the best possible final game, running on that pitch and celebrating with my wonderful teammates and all the work we put in through a tricky year.”

Despite winning the Europa League, it was a complicated campaign for Spurs, as they slumped to their worst ever Premier League season, finishing 17th and losing 22 of their 38 league games.

Spurs dropped everything to end their trophy drought, and manager Ange Postecoglu paid with his job, sacked 16 days after the final despite staying true to his promise to deliver silverware in his second season.

Simultaneously “within and without” as the Great Gatsby narrator, Nick Carraway, once famously quipped, Whiteman held a unique position in Spurs’ squad during his final season.

People think they know a lot about [football] but the reality of it within the walls of the training ground is probably quite different

He was aware he was never likely to influence the game on the pitch, yet understood he had a role to play in the dressing room and on the training ground as they stood on the cusp of history.

“I do feel football is something that people think they know a lot about but the reality of it within the walls of the training ground is probably quite different,” Whiteman asserts. “Everyone wins together and suffers together.”

Retirement was already in Whiteman’s plans as he rushed onto the pitch in Bilbao. Four years earlier, he captured over 600 vulnerable self-portraits and diary entries that encapsulated the solitude, loneliness, and self-exploration of his loan spell with Swedish club Degerfors IF.

These insights would form the basis of his first formal step into the arts, as his exhibition ‘A Loan’ was showcased at the OOF Gallery inside the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

“It wasn’t a project made with the idea of it being exhibited. It was purely out of this time of searching for purpose, frustration with self, feeling like I’m down a path that maybe isn’t the one I want to do and dealing with insecurities and imposter syndrome.

“It was just reflecting upon all those things of self-doubt, so it was quite surreal, actually. It was nice that it was resonating with people.”

Influenced by his parents, who were always “encouraging art and expression”, and his upbringing in cosmopolitan London, Whiteman is also a major film buff and regularly heads to the BFI Southbank or the Prince Charles Cinema in Leicester Square.

He recently attended the BFI’s London Film Festival, where the comedy-drama Club Kid was among the screenings to catch his attention. If there was one film to sum up his time at Spurs, though?

“Wow, that’s a tricky question,” he chuckles before a clinical concentration becomes etched across his face as if stepping up to save the winning penalty in the World Cup final.

“Wim Wenders’ (1987 romantic fantasy) Wings of Desire but maybe (Wenders’ 2023 Japanese-language drama) Perfect Days, one of his more recent films.

“I think (in Perfect Days) it was this real appreciation of life itself and the small things, and not getting caught up in all the stresses we have and just taking a step back and appreciating how lucky we are, which I think that film really encapsulates.

“It’s about really finding purpose in what you’re doing, and that sort of beauty of the small everyday things.”

#1846. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision.  We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

It’s full time at GTech Stadium: Brentford 1 Sunderland 1

Pierre Sage has his first win while Alvaro Arbeloa has lost his first three Premier League games and go to Anfield next Saturday. Frank de Boer vibes.

City needed Donnarumma to spare their blushes with several good saves.

Brighton 1 Leeds 1. Pascal Gross missed a late sitter and Leeds are still winless in Brighton’s ‘new’ stadium in 11 visits.

It remains 0-0 so Spurs are goalless in three, both sides remain winless.

Iliman Ndiaye took a knock and has come off after treatment. He has sat on the bench, though, rather than headed down the tunnel, which suggests it is not an injury.

Enzo Le Fee equalises from the penalty spot.

VAR does not intervene after Lewis-Potter was penalised for holding. Le Fee chipped a pen straight at the keeper there last season.

Ellis Simms with the latest, clocking Donnarumma flush in the face with his close-range effort.

And it’s a third goal from a  left-back, but this time it’s the substitute Ben Chilwell.

Jaidon Anthony bundled the ball in but had used his hands.

Big cheer for Phil Foden when he came on for Rayan Cherki. Cherki has been creative for City and this might be trying another mode of attack for Enzo Maresca or saving legs for the Champions League in midweek. They have two full days of rest before facing Porto on Tuesday.

That is a big chance for Coventry. Loum Tchaouna got room in the penalty area and it needed Gianluigi Donnarumma to save low to his right.

Luka Vuskovic heads in from an inswinging corner.

Controversy at the City Ground – and it’s again a result of Var.

Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Neco Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goalline.

The goal did go to Var for a possible handball by Williams, and it was ruled that the Wales international did handle it. Did look very harsh.

Coventry are still in this game but City have their chances to put them away. Enzo was deemed offside when he set up a strike for Haaland. The UK’s most expensive player has got better during this game.

Looks like it will be ruled out for handball.

Vitaly Janelt breaks the deadlock after Brentford were battered in the first half.

Keith Andrews is a brave manager. Having been forced into a change after 17 minutes when his captain, Nathan Collisn was injured, he shook it up at half-time by replacing three of his biggest signings, Kayode, Sangaré and Ouattara for Hickey, Yarmoliuk and Anthony.

There might be a VAR check but Neco Williams is in like Flynn when Tonali makes a bad mistake.

Mohammed Kudus comes on for Sávio and Andy Robertson for Destiny Udogie.

Igor Jesus and Daniel Muñoz come on for Ola Aina and Dan Ndoye.

Tyrick Mitchell has scored his second. What do they say about London buses…

Mitchell rampaging up the left, shoots. It’s blocked by García who tries to clear by hitting it straight into Mitchell’s foot whence it ricochets past Bernd Leno.

It was the culmination of a long passage of huffing and puffing after Marmoush had scudded a free-kick straight into the Forest wall.

Forest are clinging on a bit at the moment with some pretty desperate defending.

It was put in by Jacob Strand Larsen, who came on for Eddie Nketiah at half-time but he was offside.

With Tottenham appearing so toothless in attack, you have to wonder whether Roberto De Zerbi ends the long wait for Mykhailo Mudryk.

It is over 600 days since Mudryk last played a competitive match.

There is also the option of Dominic Solanke on the bench too.

Tanaka was offside when he turned in Stach’s free-kick. Leeds squander opportunity to double their lead.

Because of the 4½ minute VAR check for the Ballard ‘goal’ and an injury to Nathan Collins that forced the Bees’ captain off.

These are clearly two teams in transition.

Tottenham have spent over £300m this summer and are still waiting for lift-off.

Forest are embarking on a new era under Oliver Glasner with a style of play that will take time to implement.

It’s been a messy game so far with both teams struggling to impose themselves.

The best chance fell to one of Tottenham’s new arrivals, Omar Marmoush, but he drilled a shot wide of the post.

Josh King scores one and makes one. César Palacios with the rebound after Gonzalo García’s effort was parried to him.

Oliver Glasner’s wife Bettina is making her first visit to the City Ground today.

Glasner said that he is hoping to celebrate dinner tonight with his first three points since taking charge.

In a ding-dong match, the left-back, Tyrick Mitchell, pounces to fire Palace level.

Lewis Dunk saves Brighton after Calvert-Lewin had rounded Verbruggen and tried to slide it in on the angle.

Erling Haaland at the back post with a thunderous header – his 300th goal in club football.

Kamada was offside by a gnat’s whisker. VAR is making this job ridiculous.

Coventry fans are in good voice – and jeering Enzo Fernandez when he gets the ball. The Argentina midfielder has been quiet so far.

Messy start here at the City Ground with both teams struggling for fluency.

Tottenham are still waiting for their first goal of the season with a drastically reshaped team.

Danso was deemed to be interfering with play in an offside position, blocking the goalkeeper’s view of Ballard’s strike.

Disasi gives the ball away to Charles who finds Bobb. His pass sets up King for a shot which is deflected past Henderson.

Kevin Danso was standing in front of Kelleher in an offside position.

Cherki makes headway down the left and sends over a dipping, menacing cross towards Enzo who is pushed high as a No10 but Carl Rushworth plucks it out of the air.

It’s Enzo Fernández replacing Nico O’Reilly not Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Enzo Fernandez will start, it has been confirmed, with O’Reilly injured in the warm-up

Fernandez is lined up in the tunnel ready to come out.

England left-back, who was slated to play in midfield, hurt his back/hip in the warm-up.

Seems to have a problem with his lower back or hip. He has been ruled out of the match.

The big headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

#1845. GdS: Linear structure and a strong work force – what Krösche is likely to implement at Milan

AC Milan are expected to hire Markus Krösche in the next few weeks, and a report has looked a little more at his work today.

Between Eintracht Frankfurt and Milan, there are plenty of differences. From the finances available to how they’re spent, even to the way in which the structure of the club ticks over. So, Krösche will have to learn with the Rossoneri.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, it won’t be a one way street, with the Diavolo needing to learn plenty too.

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, Krösche methods are very linear; it’s about arriving and leaving at the right time, having the knowledge to enter and the courage to step away when the time is right.

His belief is that the club will always hold more weight than the manager, which has been shown in the past few months by Gerry Cardinale and there is no shortage of exciting signings on his CV.

What is also worth remembering is that he’s not one to step away from his methods. In 2022, he was given a chance to sign Cristiano Ronaldo. However, it didn’t make sense for him or Frankfurt, so they never made their move.

If it happens his way, Timmo Hardung will arrive alongside the German. The pair met at RB Leipzig and their relationship has only grown since then and Krösche eventually led a team of 70 people at Frankfurt. In other words, he won’t be out of place at the top of the Milan football organisation.

Gazzetta even suggests that it’s ‘no secret’ that his desire is to move to Italy to work under Krösche once again. Given their successes together, it makes sense why all parties are hoping to keep that relationship under the same roof.

#1844. Mikel Arteta has Arsenal stars looking as hungry as ever with rest of season predicted

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal hold a five-point lead at the top of the Premier League table.

A 3-0 loss at the Amex Stadium against Brighton was the only one of their ten matches so far this season in which they have dropped points in the league.

With 10 points from a possible 12 in the Champions League as well, it has been near enough as good a start as Mikel Arteta and his players could have wished for.

The defeat away at Brighton was a horror show and the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood was embarrassing, but otherwise it was a superb start to the season for Arsenal.

They have, on the whole, played better football than last season, even if many matches have not had the margin to make it feel more comfortable.

Arsenal went toe-to-toe with Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arena, a performance that should give them real confidence when the knockout stages of the Champions League come around.

It has been a tough run of fixtures to start the season, with so many difficult away trips already ticked off, and Arsenal have come through that sitting pretty.

Ezri Konsa has been by far the standout of the summer additions. He has slotted into the defence seamlessly and made an already formidable backline look effectively impenetrable.

There can be no greater compliment to Konsa than the fact he has given Arteta a major selection headache now William Saliba is fit again.

Bruno Guimaraes' best moments have come off the bench, with goals against Sunderland and Leeds. He has thrived when things have been more desperate and there is a chaotic edge to the match.

When starting alongside Declan Rice, Guimaraes has looked far less comfortable and his lack of mobility has been exposed on several occasions.

Further up the pitch, Christos Tzolis made a bright start to life at the club before missing a month with a hamstring injury.

It is still hard not to look at the summer transfer window as a huge missed opportunity in attack. Arsenal needed to do much more.

Arsenal legend and double winner Peter Storey dies aged 81

Arsenal starlet sent off as England U19s routed on nightmare outing

Jury remains out on Alonso amid Chelsea progress with season predicted

Konsa aside, it feels like the form this season is in spite of the business done in that window rather than because of it.

He did not get the statement attacking signing he wanted in the summer but Mikel Arteta has not let that slow Arsenal down.

After the mental and physical toll last season took on the squad, followed by many of them spending the summer at the World Cup, there was a strong chance that Arsenal could have stumbled into the new season.

That has not happened. Arteta has got his players looking as hungry as ever and the start to the league campaign has been brilliant.

The one criticism of Arteta would still be how he manages certain players. He has rotated this season, particularly in Europe, but it still feels as though unnecessary risks are sometimes taken.

Did Declan Rice need to play 90 minutes against Slavia Prague, for example? Gabriel, too, is surely in need of a rest soon.

I backed Arsenal to defend their crown in the summer and see no reason to change that stance now.

The defence has got even better and this is a squad remarkable in its depth, capable of dealing with injuries in key positions.

With the uncertainty surrounding Manchester City, and the likes of Chelsea and Liverpool looking extremely unconvincing, Arsenal are by far the club in the best shape to win the title again.

#1843. When will Thomas Frank take charge of first Crystal Palace game? Eagles ‘finalising’ appointment of Pierre Sage replacement

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 12:32, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 12:34

Crystal Palace are reportedly close to appointing Thomas Frank as their new head coach.

The Eagles appear to be moving quickly to replace Pierre Sage, who was sacked last Thursday after less than five months in charge.

It had previously been reported that Sean Dyche was the ‘frontrunner’ to replace Sage, while the likes of Anthony Barry, Vitor Pereira, Rob Edwards, Jens Berthel Askou and Ole Werner have also been linked with the Eagles job.

However, former Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur boss Frank has now been identified as the leading candidate to take the reins at Selhurst Park, with ‘advanced talks’ held over the weekend.

The Athletic have since claimed that Palace are finalising an agreement to appoint Frank, who is expected to become the club’s new head coach.

Talks are said to be ongoing over Frank’s backroom staff and an official announcement of his arrival in South London is set to follow in due course.

All being well, Frank could potentially take charge of his first Crystal Palace game on Saturday when they travel to Coventry City in the Premier League.

If Frank is not appointed before the weekend, then the Dane could instead make his Palace debut in the Europa League when the Eagles play host to Real Sociedad on November 26.

The 53-year-old is set to return to management for the first time since he was sacked by Tottenham in February after only eight months in charge.

Frank won just 13 of his 38 matches with Spurs and left the club languishing in 16th place in the Premier League table, five points above the relegation zone.

He had previously enjoyed a successful seven-year spell as Brentford boss between 2018 and 2025, steering the Bees into the top flight and then establishing them as a competitive Premier League outfit, reaching a ninth-place finish in 2023.

In June, Frank stated that he had no intentions to take a new managerial position, but he now appears to be ready to return to the dugout and embark on a fresh challenge with Crystal Palace.

Frank will be tasked with lifting the Eagles off the foot of the Premier League table following a run of seven defeats in 10 games at the start of this season under Sage, conceding a division-high 24 goals in the process.

However, victory over Coventry this weekend could see Palace climb out of the relegation zone and up to 16th in the table if other results were to go their way.

#1842. Why the jury remains out on Xabi Alonso despite Chelsea progress with rest of season predicted

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea have made progress under Xabi Alonso in some areas but in others still look the same chaotic team Enzo Maresca and then Liam Rosenior presided over.

They sit fifth in the table at present and boast one of the Premier League’s most thrilling attacks yet have also dropped points against Hull and lost to both Tottenham and Sunderland, who were bottom of the table at the time.

As the November international break draws to a close, it is time to reassess the progress they have made and the direction of travel under Alonso.

Chelsea’s season began with strong form but in truth has very much been a mixed bag so far.

The victories over Fulham, Brighton, Bournemouth and Leeds (in the Carabao Cup) have shown Chelsea at their free-flowing best, but only twice have they kept a Premier League clean sheet so far and there are defensive weaknesses that either need solving or, failing that, disguising by Alonso and his team in the months ahead.

The penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool that saw Chelsea exit the Carabao Cup early was a real disappointment in a season when there is no European football to be had, and it is understandable why plenty of Chelsea fans remain unsure quite what Alonso’s team are and what they want to be, even though they sit fifth in the league.

They have been beaten by Tottenham and Sunderland, neither of which should be games they are losing.

Chelsea made 10 first-team signings in the summer as they totally revamped their squad ready for Alonso’s first season in charge.

By far the best performer among their summer recruits has been Morgan Rogers, who has 11 goal contributions in 13 games for the Blues since his £117million arrival from Aston Villa during the World Cup.

Even though they failed to sign Lamine Camara from Monaco on deadline day, they did make other recruitments that have looked like proving shrewd signings, including Valentin Barco, Pep Chavarria, Jordan Henderson and Maxence Lacroix.

It is too early to judge the likes of Danny Welbeck, Emi Martinez and Geovany Quenda. Marco Palestra has been disappointing so far.

It has been a reasonable but not spectacular start to life at Chelsea for Alonso. There have been some decent wins under the Spaniard but also some poor defending and a few performances where it was difficult to detect his tactical influence.

Arteta keeps Arsenal stars hungry as rest of season predicted

Alex Scott told to reject £100m Chelsea transfer as Arsenal handed boost

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal revive Vinicius talks; Man Utd want Hall

He has kept his cards close to his chest when speaking to the media but this has felt at times to be a slight obstacle to him developing the strong relationship with Chelsea fans that he and they no doubt want. So has not playing Estevao more.

His team selections were poor against Spurs and Sunderland. It is still early doors for Alonso, who continues to insist Chelsea will look very difficult by the time the season is drawing to a close in May.

At the beginning of the season I predicted that Chelsea would finish fourth, but I have not seen enough from them yet to convince me they will finish quite that high. We’re talking small margins, though, and over the course of 38 league games I do believe they will be good enough to sneak into the Champions League with a fifth-place finish, providing England can claim one of the extra European slots as it always seems to.

Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer, Moises Caicedo and Rogers staying fit for the bulk of the season is imperative if they are to return to Europe’s premier competition. If those key men do remain available at Alonso’s disposal, they should gradually improve.
