#1776. Cardinale clarifies his ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ statement: “Lead the club into a new era”

Gerry Cardinale has clarified his ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ statement from about three years ago, stating that investments and resources are needed to get AC Milan back to the top.

Back in September 2023, a little over a year after he completed the purchase of Milan, Cardinale sat down with Corriere della Sera to explain his project for the club. “In football I want to be a Berlusconi 2.0, to have the same impact as him in a completely changed context,” he said, among other things.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s a quote that didn’t land brilliantly with some of the Milan fans, who felt that Cardinale grossly underestimated how much work Berlusconi put in with the throwaway comment. It was more than just a throwaway comment, though.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, following the launch of Milan’s new holding company MSE, Cardinale clarified what he meant by the quote. It was not meant as an arrogant comparison, but rather as praise for Berlusconi and what he can learn from the legendary Milan owner.

The connection with Milan deserves a separate mention: RedBird and the city are now even more connected…

“This is the legacy we will leave in Milan. The stadium, obviously, represents a huge legacy that will transform our financial profile, but then there’s also the San Donato development project and the rest.

“If we want AC Milan to become great again, we need to close the revenue gap with the Premier League clubs. When I bought the club four years ago, I used the expression ‘Berlusconi 2.0’ and no one understood what I meant. Now perhaps we are starting to see it.”

“Everyone thought I was making an arrogant, self-centred comparison between me and Berlusconi, but that wasn’t my point. What I was trying to explain was that, just as Berlusconi transformed AC Milan and Serie A, we want to be able, through our ownership, to lead the club into a new era.

“We need to do it in the same way Berlusconi did, albeit in a modern way. I’m used to working a certain way because that’s how I do things, at the highest levels worldwide and in America.”

#1775. Everton transfer news: Jack Grealish replacement emerges with Toffees among ‘top contenders’ for 21 G/A winger

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 18:19

Everton have identified Flamengo winger Samuel Lino as a possible transfer target, according to a report.

The Toffees are expected to bolster their squad in the January after enduring a frustrating end to the summer transfer window, selling Iliman Ndiaye, Beto and Tim Iroegbunam on Deadline Day without bringing in a replacement.

While the addition of a new centre-forward to ease the burden on Thierno Barry is thought to be among Everton’s main priorities, pursuing a new winger may also be high on the agenda for manager David Moyes.

The long-term future of Manchester City loanee Jack Grealish has come under the spotlight following his ‘breach of club discipline’ prior to the international break.

Tyrique George has since stepped up in Grealish’s absence on the left flank, while fellow wingers Brennan Johnson and Tyler Dibling have struggled to reach the heights expected on a consistent basis for some time.

According to Swiss news outlet 4-4-2, via the Liverpool Echo, Everton are among a number of 'top contenders' in the race to sign Brazil international Lino, along with Paris Saint-Germain, Juventus and Napoli.

The report adds that Roma – who along with Everton are owned by The Friedkin Group – recently saw a €25m (£20.9m) offer for Lino rejected by Flamengo.

Lino has established himself as a prolific winger with Flamengo this season, scoring 12 goals and providing nine assists in 33 Brazilian Serie A appearances.

The 26-year-old was not called up to Brazil’s squad for the November international break, but he did represent Carlo Ancelotti’s side last month and scored his first two goals from his country in a 4-0 friendly win over India.

Lino is thriving in his homeland having previously spent five-and-a-half years in Europe with Gil Vicente, Atletico Madrid and Valencia.

After scoring 23 goals in 100 games for Portuguese side Gil Vicente, Lino made the move to Atletico in July 2022 before spending a season on loan at Valencia, chipping in with eight goals and three assists in 41 matches.

Lino was then integrated into Diego Simeone’s Atletico side and made 65 La Liga appearances across two seasons, but he opted to return to Brazil in January 2025, joining Flamengo for a then club-record €22m (£18.4m) and signing a four-year contract.

With several big European clubs said to be interested in Lino, the winger may be tempted by a return to Europe heading into the prime years of his career.

Meanwhile, Everton are reportedly ready to battle fellow Premier League side Nottingham Forest for a £12.5m-rated centre-back from Brazil.

#1774. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. They have been playing together forever. We find another comeback after Nottingham Forest, after Newcastle. We still have this thing to improve in the beginning of the games, but I am happy as we have shown some character. This is the Champions League, you do not have easy games.”

"You can see he's football mad." ⚽Steven Gerrard on Andoni Iraola's passion and the impact he's making at Liverpool 👏🎙️ @laura_woodsy | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/M3qKhxt8HE

There is the final whistle at Anfield and Liverpool start their Champions League campaign with a 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid. Liverpool did fall behind to Marcos Llorente’s goal but goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Alexis Mac Allister give Andoni Iraola a win in his first Champions League game as a manager.

Victory in MD1 🤩 #UCL pic.twitter.com/SWFFhSudFJ

First Champions League game. First Champions League win for Andoni Iraola ✅ pic.twitter.com/D3CE6w6V0b

Koumas is tripped by Le Normand and that should be it.

That is a silly foul from Lookman, with Frimpong inside his own box running back towards his own goal, but Lookman decides to push him in the back.

Liverpool think they have sealed it through Frimpong but the offside flag has gone up. First Munoz cuts onto his right and has a shot saved by Oblak. The ball falls to Frimpong, who slots home but he was clearly offside when Munoz took the initial shot.

Kerkez is currently down with cramp and his night is done. He will be replaced by Tsimikas and Liverpool will make their final change at the same time. Koumas comes on for Isak.

Atletico win a corner but it all stems from sloppy play in the centre of the pitch from Gravenberch. He has had a few sloppy moments since coming on.

The corner is flicked on by Hjulmand but ends up coming to nothing.

It isn’t the headline making performance, by any means, but that shouldn’t dilute the importance of Ronald Araujo’s contribution for Liverpool tonight and, indeed, against Ipswich last Friday. He’s doing what Liverpool wanted him to, providing versatility and leadership in their back four and - more than anything - quality. He hasn’t put a foot wrong.

Atletico win a corner out on the left in front of their travelling supporters. Grimaldo’s outswinger is flicked on by the head of Hancko at the near post but it goes over.

Isak has the chance to potentially seal the victory for Liverpool but Le Normand makes a crucial block. Le Normand has only just come on but already made a couple of defensive actions.

Liverpool win a corner out on the left with the last touch coming off Pubill, who was marking Van Dijk from a free-kick. Szoboszlai’s inswinger is headed away by Le Normand.

Digeo Simeone is making his final two substitutions of the night as Le Normand and Hjulmad replace Romero and Barrios,

Atletico bring on David, on loan from Juventus, for Baena.

Alvarez has a chance inside the Liverpool box but his shot is straight at Alisson. There are some appeals for handball but it hit Munoz from such close range that it is never a penalty.

Liverpool are making a substitution as Mac Allister, who scored the goal to put Liverpool in front, is replaced by Gravenberch. Mac Allister, who made some comments in the press conference yesterday about his sadness at not being offered a new contract, put in a good performance in the centre of Liverpool’s midfield. He was on a booking though so probably sensible to take him off when you can guarantee that the Atletico players would have tried to get him sent off.

We’ll see what happens in the coming weeks and months but there have been glimmers here with Florian Wirtz looking better than he has done with pace to pass to; if it clicks with him, Bradley Barcola & Alexander Isak it could be exciting but one game must be built on. It’s frustrating that Barcola’s night has ended with what appears to be cramp or tightness in his calf because he was getting more joy than he had done before half-time. The big challenge for Liverpool, too, is whether they have the nous to see this contest out.

The new Netherlands boss Xavi is in attendance at Anfield tonight, watching the likes of Van Dijk, Frimpong and Gravenberch, although the latter is still yet to come off the Liverpool bench.

This is a concern for Liverpool. Barcola has gone down and seems to have some pain in his left calf. Is it cramp or an injury? It will be a double change for the home side as Frimpong and Munoz come on. Barcola is given a standing ovation as he goes off and the Liverpool fans will be hoping it is just cramp. Ngumoha also heads off.

Diego Simeone is going to make his first two changes of the night. Grimaldo and Lookman come on

It is all Liverpool as they sense a third goal is there for the taking. Ngumoha does well down Liverpool’s left and pushes it past Pubill, who slides in and takes him down. Pubill is booked. He cannot believe it but I do not know why; a clear foul and yellow card.

That is a stunning strike from the Argentine. The ball falls to the midfielder just outside the box and he hits it first time. He hits the ball so crisply and there is nothing Oblak can do to stop it. Liverpool should have taken the lead through Barcola moments before they do now have the lead for the first time tonight.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

Well, that’s one way to prove you might warrant a new contract. A quite beautiful left footed drive from Alexis Mac Allister gives Liverpool the lead and it has been noticeable thus far in Andoni Iraola’s matches that his team get stronger at the start of the second period. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. It is the perfect counter-attack really from Liverpool and it is Wirtz and Barcola who exchange passes from deep inside their own half all the way to the Atletico penalty area. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

We are back under way at Anfield. No changes from either side at the break.

Some of the statistics are pretty even but Atletico Madrid have had just three touches in the Liverpool penalty area, yet have a goal to their name.

The first half at Anfield is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break. Llorente gave Atletico the lead before Szoboszlai equalised for Liverpool. The home fans let the officials know what they think of their performance in that first half.

One added minute at the end of this first half.

There has been about five minutes of squabbling between the Liverpool and Atletico benches, so much so that Tommy Elphick - Andoni Iraola’s assistant - missed Dominik Szoboszlai score the equaliser. Tensions have only increased after a nasty little challenge from Cristian Romero on Alexander Isak. The half-time whistle might be coming at a good time to defuse the situation but you fancy the walk back to the dressing rooms will be spicy.

The conduct of the Atletico players is frankly embarrassing, not a massive surprise from a Diego Simeone side. Kang goes down clutching his face when there was barely any contact and then, unlike Isak, he does not have to spend a minute off the pitch.

Isak is on the ground, clutching at his knee, after a heavy challenge from Romero. It is a nasty challenge from Romero, who remarkably is neither booked nor penalised. To compound the awful officiating, Isak now has to spend a minute off the pitch owing to the new rules. What do you make of that new rule of the player who is down going off for a minute? Have your say in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Moments after Liverpool equalised, Atletico have a decent opportunity to restore their lead but Baena drags his effort wide from the edge of the box.

Moments after Barcola could not take a big chance to equalise for Liverpool, Szoboslzai does. First, Barcola is denied by Oblak. Liverpool keep it alive inside the Atletico box and a simple sensational flick by Aruajo finds Szoboszlai, who finds the bottom corner with a clinical finish. Kerkez has been poor tonight but he deserves credit for his part in that goal as he was the player to initially win it back for Liverpool with a good press.

Szoboszlai slots home after a brilliant flick from Araujo! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrHQTwtgsY

Liverpool look like a team that has been out of the Champions League for a couple of years and are only just finding its feet, which seems strange given they missed only one year in the last 10. They have glimmers of promise but they aren’t convincing anyone they will blow Atleti’s house down. One day everything will align for Atleti and they will reach another final. They have an outside chance this year, especially if Julian Alvarez - easily the best player on this pitch - has anything to do with it. Diego Simeone always has class strikers at the top of his team and Alvarez stands comparison with any who have gone before.

Wirtz has a great chance to equalise for Liverpool but his shot on the half volley is saved by Oblak. It would not have mattered anyway had the ball ended up in the net because Isak was offside before crossing for Wirtz.

Some of the officiating tonight has been appalling and the latest example is VAR taking a check on a possible red card for Mac Allister for a foul that is never a red card in a million years. The officials then take an age to give yet another obvious offside and, in the end, the referee gives it rather than the linesman. That really does sum up the officials tonight as the referee should not be the one to give offsides.

Alvarez shoots from distance and forces Alisson into a good save diving to his right. There was a suspicion of offside from Simeone in the build-up.

Atletico take it short but Simeone’s shot is blocked by Araujo.

What a save from Alisson! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PuajED3Rks

The Anfield faithful are furious. Two fouls in quick succession are not given when they were both clearly fouls. The referee appears to have a different interpretation of body checks and taking people out off the ball than the rest of us.

The Spanish side take the lead at Anfield and it is another goal on this ground for Llorente. Alvarez feeds a through ball to pick out the run of Llorente, who is onside. He takes one touch before firing past Alisson from the edge of the box. That is poor, poor defending from Kerkez, who not only played Llorente onside but then did not track the run properly. Llorente now has five goals on this ground.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

The idea that Atletico Madrid are focused on spoiling and nullifying belongs in the past. They are an attractive team, well organised and you suspect they have the gears to cause Liverpool problems... and as we type, they have just opened the scoring by playing straight through Liverpool’s middle. It was a bad goal for home side to concede. Milos Kerkez was out of sync with the rest of Liverpool’s defence and Marcos Llorente has galloped straight through. As we said at the start: it’s a big test for the hosts... it’s just got even bigger.

A little line about Llorente, who has now scored five times against Liverpool in the Champions League. He is fond of playing in this arena, he named his dog “Anfield! when he bought it in 2021.

Chance for Barcola. Szoboszlai clips a lovely ball in behind down the right channel to pick out the run of Barcola. The Frenchman takes it down beautifully before having his shot saved by Oblak. Barcola’s best moment thus far tonight.

Baena takes a first-time effort on from a central position around 25 yards out but he cannot keep his effort down and it sails into The Kop.

Atletico were renowned for years under Diego Simeone is being very tight at the back and in midfield, especially away from home. However, in recent years they have become more expansive and as a result are more open.

Liverpool win their first corner of the night at the Anfield Road End in front of the travelling Atletico fans. They take it short and Szoboslzai takes it towards the Atletico box. It appeared to be a very obvious foul on Szoboszlai right on the edge of the box but nothing is given. At the very least, it should have been given a free-kick as there was definitely at least one foul.

Barcola, who has won the Champions League with PSG in the last two seasons, is starting out on the right for Liverpool tonight with Ngumoha on the left.

Big test for Liverpool and it will be fascinating to see how this formation works out. It looks very much like it is 4-4-2, with Florian Wirtz almost alongside Alexander Isak and Rio Ngumoha the left winger and Bradley Barcola on the opposite flank - a position Andoni Iraola has referenced him playing in Lyon as a teenager. It’s also a big test for Iraola against Diego Simeone, the wily and vastly experienced manager, who is immaculately dressed - as always - in his trademark black suit.

Liverpool have a chance inside the opening minute. Szoboszlai wins it inside his own half and drives forward. He then plays it out to his right to find Isak, whose shot from the right side of the box is dragged wide of the far post. Isak did score from a similar position against Ipswich last Friday, when he scored at the near post.

A minute’s silence to remember the victims of the landslides in Nepal is impeccably observed.

We are under way at Anfield. Liverpool’s Champions League campaign gets going as Andoni Iraola takes charge of his first game as a manager in this competition.

The two sides emerge from the tunnel to a cacophony of noise and we are moments away from kick-off at Anfield. The home fans boo the Champions League anthem and belt out “Liverpool! Liverpool!” over the top of it. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

The original “This is Anfield” sign has sold at auction for almost £150,000, 10 times more than its guide price.

The sign that hung above the players’ tunnel at Liverpool’s home stadium during the 1970s had been expected to fetch between £10,000 and £15,000 after being put up for auction on Tuesday and Wednesday.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

The Dutchman has been in fine form at the start of the season for Liverpool, registering a goal and three assists in his first three games. He missed training yesterday and is not in Liverpool’s matchday squad tonight. Andoni Iraola has confirmed that Gakpo has a small adductor injury that he picked up in the Ipswich game last Friday but could be fit for the weekend against Fulham.

Liverpool: Alisson; Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak.Substitutes: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Tsimikas, Munoz, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Chambers, McConnell, Koumas, Danns.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. But we have to get used to this; it is what big clubs do. Definitely there is part of your mind where you have to think [about] the next games. But for us, the game tomorrow is very important.”

Ready for #UCL action 👊🔴 pic.twitter.com/XyOupLwsRe

Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

#1773. ‘Mission accomplished’ – Hallgrimsson revels in Ireland’s second-place finish

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson declared it was "mission accomplished" for his team after they secured second spot in Nations League Group B3 with a 3-0 win over 10-man Kosovo.

Ireland went into the game knowing they needed to win to leapfrog Kosovo in the table, and they were given an early boost when Kreshnik Hajrizi was shown a straight red card 26 minutes in for a handball on the line.

It was Troy Parrott's header that he kept out, and the striker stepped up to convert the resulting penalty.

Ireland continued to dominate but had to wait until the 50th minute for their second goal when Parrott was felled in the box by Arijanet Muric, and the striker again confidently swept in from the spot.

Kosovo, who had made a bright start before the red card, offered little in terms of a fightback, and Jack Moylan made sure of the win in the 75th minute when he glanced his header past Muric.

And Hallgrimsson was thrilled his side managed to accomplish their initial goal.

"Mission accomplished, task completed," he told RTE.

"It's nice to say that, as it doesn't happen often for these guys, but now they need to get used to that.

"They [Kosovo] started throwing themselves down, shouting, screaming, but we talked about that before the game, to stay focused and switched on – don't get over ambitious. We didn't score in the beginning but kept on going.

"Even in the second half, sometimes when you're 1-0 up, you start to cheat and don't go when you need to go, but we went man for man with a high press. I think that was a good decision, and the players executed it perfectly."

3-0 win, a Nations League Promotion Play-Off place & Pot 2 for UEFA Euro 2028 Qualifying secured  https://t.co/aLhJ0A8kYg

— Ireland Football  (@IrelandFootball) November 17, 2026

Ireland could have had more goals, having 28 shots overall, with 12 of those hitting the target, as they accumulated 4.6 expected goals (xG).

They also had seven Opta-defined 'big' chances, and 40 touches in the opposition box, while facing just five Kosovo attempts at the other end worth 0.2 xG.

The victory means Ireland will enter the League A/B play-offs in March as they aim to try and gain promotion to the top tier of the competition.

"The goal for this Nations League was to achieve that second place and pot two in the draw," Hallgrimsson added.

"To have a play-off game against a good nation is a bonus, and hopefully we will be in a group of four teams for the Euro [qualifiers], and this makes it more likely, not a group of five."

#1772. Man United transfer news: Mauricio Pochettino addresses claims he could target USA players for Red Devils

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 18:25, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 18:28

Incoming Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has refused to be drawn on suggestions that the club could target USA players in the upcoming transfer windows.

Pochettino is leaving his role with the USA in order to take charge of Man United.

The Argentine is expected to arrive in England on Wednesday morning after managing the United States in the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti.

Since being appointed head coach of the 20-time English champions, there have been suggestions that Man United could look to target players who are well-known to Pochettino from his time in charge of the national side.

Juventus' Weston McKennie, Villarreal's Alex Freeman, Bournemouth's Tyler Adams and Monaco's Folarin Balogun are among those to be linked with switches.

"Now is not the time [to talk about this]. All the good players always have dreams to reach the highest level. And I think Man United is one of the teams that is in the highest level and it's the dream for many of the players," Pochettino told reporters.

"But now, I think they need to be focused on today, on tomorrow's game, on their clubs. I know really well for more than two years every single player.

"And I think they are all players with unbelievable talent. Of course, in the future, when that happens, of course we are going to pay attention, you know, to make some decisions and to pay attention to players that we know really well."

McKennie, who has previously played in the Premier League for Leeds United, also discussed the possibility of some of the national team's players making the move to Man United.

"I think obviously his time here, I think he's obviously grown to like this team and seen the quality that this team has to offer," he said during a pre-match press conference.

"And yeah, I think it's a potential. I think we have a lot of guys on our team that are due to probably make moves soon or within the next year. And so I think it's kind of inevitable.

"But at the end of the day, you never know what's going on in a coach's mind and what players that he's actually looking for. But I think he could potentially see some of the guys from here being talked about to go to Man U and potentially it happening."

Pochettino has a record of 22 wins, two draws and 12 defeats from his 36 matches in charge of the United States.

#1771. Napoli 3-3 AC Milan Women: Lead lost twice as Rossonere claim just one point

AC Milan Women were held to a 3-3 draw in their away game against Napoli on Saturday afternoon, despite having the lead twice.

It has been a rough start to the season for Suzanne Bakker and her side, clinching a mere seven points in the first seven games. Even worse, the form seems to be declining as with today’s game included, they haven’t won in the last three games (1D, 2L).

In the derby against Inter last week, the Rossonere only had themselves to blame for the 0-3 defeat after missing several good chances, while conceding two penalties and getting a red card. They didn’t exactly make things better today either.

After just five minutes of play, the former Milan player Chante Dompig opened the scoring for the hosts. In fairness to the Rossonere, it was a cracking finish from outside the box to stun Sally Rainey in goal, so not much could be done.

Milan responded in the best way possible as Sara Kanutte Fornes pounced on a huge mistake by the Napoli defence, tapping in the equaliser after 16 minutes of play. Just ten minutes later, Abi Brighton found the striker on a corner, heading it home nicely for an early brace.

The Rossonere played well after that and headed into the break with a 2-1 lead. It wasn’t a poor start to the second half, but in the 58th minute, a really poor offside trap (of sorts) meant Napoli only had to play one pass to play Kinga Kozak through, and she made no mistakes.

Sloppy defending that Milan thought they had cancelled out in the 78th minute after a lovely move. Thea Kyvåg found Christy Grimshaw in the box with a great cross and the veteran headed it to Emma Koivisto, who in turn headed it into the back of the net.

The lead only lasted about six minutes, though, as Napoli suddenly had loads of space on the right flank and played a smart low cross into the box. Considering the lack of coverage on the flank, the Milan players at least should have kept tabs on things in the box, but they didn’t.

And so, Michela Giordano made it 3-3 and that was also the final result in the end. Two points dropped for Milan against another struggling side.

Manchester United are set to name Mauricio Pochettino as head coach to replace Michael Carrick following a day of talks over both men.

United moved closer to putting Pochettino in charge at Old Trafford after reaching a verbal agreement with the US national team boss on Wednesday. The club then made a formal approach to US Soccer.

Meanwhile, the club’s chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew back from Monaco, where minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe was expected to ratify their decision to sack Carrick with the blessing of co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer.

Carrick’s departure could be confirmed on Thursday, but official confirmation of Pochettino’s appointment may take a little longer with more talks planned overnight on Wednesday.

Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday.

It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games, with United said to be relaxed over the Argentine taking the team. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester.

Pochettino, who has managed Southampton,Tottenham, and Chelsea, will succeed Michael Carrick

Carrick checked in at Carrington at 7.45am on Wednesday with his fate in the balance

The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m.

‘I mean, the credibility, the resume speaks for itself. It goes to show for us how lucky we are to be able to work under a manager of his quality and the person he is.’

Meanwhile, Berrada and Wilcox flew back to Manchester from Nice on Wednesday with United expected to announce Carrick’s departure imminently after 10 months in charge.

The 45-year-old took training at Carrington for the second day running, arriving at 7.45am and leaving shortly after 1.30pm.

However, it has been clear for some days that Carrick would lose his job after United dropped into the relegation zone following the club’s worst start in 40 years.

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 18:39, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 19:08

Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp has made two changes to his starting lineup for this evening’s UEFA Nations League decider against the Netherlands at the Olympiastadion in Berlin.

Both changes come in defence, with centre-back Nico Schlotterbeck and left-back Nathaniel Brown coming in to replace Malick Thiaw and Maximilian Mittelstadt respectively.

Schlotterbeck and Brown are joined in a four-man backline by Philipp Treu and Jonathan Tah, protecting Ajax goalkeeper Marc-Andre ter Stegen.

Captain Joshua Kimmich will earn his 118th international cap alongside Bayern Munich teammate Aleksandar Pavlovic, with Liverpool playmaker Florian Wirtz operating in the number 10 role.

Brajan Gruda, who along with Wirtz scored in Germany's 3-1 win against Serbia last Friday, retains his starting spot in attack along with Derry Scherhant and centre-forward Kai Havertz.

Germany know that they will climb from third to first position in League A Group B if they beat the Netherlands and Greece fail to beat Serbia, while Klopp's men can secure at least a quarter-final place if they draw in Berlin and Greece lose.

As for the Netherlands, head coach Xavi has made just the one change to the side that began the 7-0 thrashing of Greece in Amsterdam last Friday.

Crystal Palace midfielder Quinten Timber has been recalled at the expense of injured Barcelona star Frenkie de Jong who sustained a back problem against Greece.

This means that Timber and his brother Jurrien Timber of Arsenal – who netted a brace against Greece – will start together for just the second time on the international stage, having previously done so against Greece in October.

In the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Denzel Dumfries will captain the Oranje at right-back, joining Jan Paul van Hecke, Micky Van de Ven and Jurrien Timber in a four-man defence playing in front of goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

Quinten Timber will link up with Joey Veerman and Tijjani Reijnders in a three-man midfield, the latter of whom netted a 33-minute first-half hat-trick against Greece.

In-form Roma striker Donyell Malen was also on the scoresheet last time out and will continue to lead the line next to fellow attackers Crysencio Summerville and Cody Gakpo, who scored a 92nd-minute equaliser in the 1-1 draw with Germany in September.

Netherlands head into this contest knowing they will finish top of their group and qualify for the Nations League quarter-finals if they avoid defeat against Germany, while they can also qualify if Greece fail to beat Serbia.

Netherlands starting lineup: Verbruggen; Dumfries, Van de Ven; Van Hecke, J. Timber; Q. Timber, Veerman, Reijnders; Summerville, Malen, Gakpo

#1767. Coritiba vs Santos - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 16 Nov 2026 20:01, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 10:52

Coritiba will be looking to move closer to securing their Campeonato Brasileiro Serie A status when they welcome Santos to the Estadio Major Antonio Couto Pereira on Wednesday.

The hosts sit 13th in the table with 42 points from 34 matches, five clear of the relegation zone, while the visitors occupy ninth place on 47 points and are hoping to strengthen their push for a place in next season's Copa Libertadores.

Coritiba head into Wednesday's encounter having lost 1-0 away to Internacional in their last league outing, with the defeat preventing them from recording consecutive victories after previously beating Vitoria 2-0 at home.

The result in Porto Alegre extended a difficult period for the Coxa, who have now recorded just one win in their last nine league matches, losing six times and drawing twice during that run.

Coritiba will be keen to make the most of home advantage and take another step towards the 45-point target they have identified for securing top-flight survival, particularly after winning their most recent home fixture.

Guilherme Bossle is expected to remain in interim charge following Fernando Seabra's dismissal, having overseen the victory against Vitoria before the narrow defeat to Internacional, and his immediate priority will be to improve the team's consistency with only three league fixtures remaining after Wednesday's match.

Santos, meanwhile, arrive in Curitiba looking to end a three-match winless run in the league, having drawn with Bahia and Palmeiras before suffering a 2-1 defeat away to Red Bull Bragantino.

The Peixe had briefly improved their position with a 2-1 victory over Fluminense, but they have since struggled to turn promising performances into wins, recording just one victory in their last six league matches (D3, L2), leaving them six points behind sixth-placed Bahia and with ground to make up in the race for continental qualification.

Cuca's side have nevertheless been more productive in front of goal, scoring 50 times in the league, with only five teams finding the net more frequently.

The head-to-head record is another reason for Santos to approach the fixture with confidence, as they have lost only once in the last 10 meetings between the clubs, winning seven and drawing two.

However, Santos were beaten by Coritiba earlier this season, suffering a 3-0 defeat on home soil, although the recent trend in this fixture favours the visitors, with the away team winning three of the last four competitive meetings.

The clubs have also met three times in 2026, including their Copa do Brasil tie, in which Santos progressed after winning 2-0 in Curitiba following a draw in the first leg.

Coritiba will be without goalkeeper Pedro Morisco, who is away with the Brazil national team and is not expected to return to Curitiba in time for Wednesday's fixture, meaning Pedro Rangel is set to start between the posts.

Defender Jacy is also a doubt after suffering a knee problem against Internacional, with the centre-back still undergoing treatment and yet to return to full training, while Lucas Ronier remains unavailable after suffering a serious knee injury.

Santos will welcome back Willian Arao and Gonzalo Escobar, who have recovered from thigh injuries and returned to unrestricted training with the first team.

Thaciano has also resumed working with the squad, although Gabriel Brazao and Lucas Veríssimo remain sidelined, while Alvaro Barreal and Vinicius Lira are also unavailable.

Gabriel Bontempo, Miguelito and Gustavo Caballero have been away on international duty, leaving Cuca with some decisions to make when selecting his squad.

Neymar is available again after having his suspension reduced, while Gabriel Barbosa is expected to lead the attack after scoring 15 goals in the 2026 Campeonato Brasileiro.

Rangel; Tinga, Tiago Coser, Moledo, B. Melo; Gomez, Santos; Lavega, Josue, Lopes; Rocha

Diogenes; Rodinei, Arao, Peres, Escobar; Henrique, Oliva; Coutinho, Neymar, Everton; Barbosa

Coritiba have the advantage of playing at home and will be encouraged by their victory over Santos earlier in the season, but their recent results have been inconsistent.

The visitors have also struggled to win recently, although they still possess enough attacking quality to find the net, making a draw a reasonable outcome.

#1766. Man United's appointment of Mauricio Pochettino feels like the Glazers are back calling the shots at Old Trafford - with Jim Ratcliffe's henchmen Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox looking like irrelevant also-rans, writes IAN HERBERT

Published: 12:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 15:14 EST, 12 November 2026

Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada once cited a line from the John Lennon song Beautiful Boy, when relating how an intended 12-month attachment at Barcelona had ended up with him staying there for 13 years. ‘Life is what happens to you while you’re busy making other plans.’

Lennon’s lyric seems far more appropriate to what Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment tells us about Berrada and his dubious grip on United, today.

While Berrada and his director of football Jason Wilcox have been busy making plans for United’s world domination – ‘to create the new history,’ as he described it to the journalist and broadcaster Andy Mitten just five months ago – it seems clear a Glazer family petrified by the shocking descent of their Premier League asset have stepped in to get Pochettino installed.

If it had been left to Berrada and Wilcox, we may have been treated to the sight of Eddie Howe wandering into the Old Trafford madhouse in the next few days. It’s been widely known and reported that Howe was Wilcox’s preference, while Christopher Vivell, director of recruitment, wanted Julian Nagelsmann.

Sources have told us that the Glazers wanted Pochettino and ordered Sir Jim Ratcliffe and his men to fall in line with that. They point to a connection between the Glazers, Pochettino and US billionaire hedge fund owner Ken Griffin.

Griffin was the main financial contributor to the salary which saw Pochettino hired by US Soccer in 2024 and again to that contract extension he signed in August. It was also Griffin, the then youthful founder of Citadel, who provided substantial funds for the Glazers’ takeover of United in 2005. Manchester United deny this, insisting that Pochettino is not a Glazer appointee.

Should Berrada and Wilcox both survive the latest embarrassment – and it would be a travesty if they do, as United pay US Soccer £7.5million in compensation for Pochettino, who would have been out of contract if they’d moved for him in August – then both will be a virtual irrelevance now. Also-rans, bypassed by the latest executive dice roll for United.

Perhaps the TV cameras will pan to them celebrating in the executive seats during some United upturn under Pochettino, weeks or months from now. If so, let it be remembered that it took the influence of others to bend things United’s way.

If Jason Wilcox (left) and Omar Berrada (right) had got their way, we would seemingly have been treated to the sight of Eddie Howe wandering into the Old Trafford madhouse

Instead the Glazers insisted that Mauricio Pochettino (pictured) would have the keys and Sir Jim Ratcliffe and his men fell in line with that

Let us not pretend there’s been any visionary executive oversight from the Glazers. They’ve already rejected Pochettino twice, in favour of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer in 2018 and Erik ten Hag four years later.

But sources close to Joel and Avram Glazer, the members of the dynasty who take some interest in their British sports asset, have indicated the brothers have been pushing to get him installed for some weeks.

The Glazers’ connection with US billionaire hedge fund owner Ken Griffin seems significant. Griffin was the main financial contributor to the salary which saw Pochettino hired by US Soccer in 2024 and again to that contract extension he signed in August.

It was also Griffin, the then youthful founder of Citadel, who provided substantial funds for the Glazers’ takeover of United in 2005.

It seems that the Old Trafford hierarchy, like so much about the club, will be skewed from now on. Pochettino does not answer to Berrada and Wilcox in the same way that Ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick have.

He transcends the structure imposed by Ratcliffe, the so-called controller of football operations, and becomes the most powerful man at Old Trafford. The individual on whose vision the futures of Berrada and Wilcox now rest. Should they stay, this is the last chance saloon for them.

United's slump in form this season has been so severe, the club have been forced to dispense with Michael Carrick just six months after giving him a two-year deal

Sources close to Avram (left) and Joel Glazer, the members of the dynasty who take some interest in United, indicate they have been pushing for Pochettino for some weeks

There should be optimism. Pochettino, more than Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, Unai Emery, Antonio Conte and all other available candidates, has the faculty, charisma and fundamental toughness to instil some mettle into United and drag the club from what Ratcliffe and Co have reduced it to. To instil the identity and culture missing for so long.

Time will only tell if he can actually make a go of the most complicated and challenging job in world football, which Ratcliffe has rendered so much harder, by stripping away so many good, essential people from the Old Trafford payroll. That really is a monumental ‘If’.

One United insider spoke for many today when observing: ‘I haven’t got a clue who can make a go of it with the people above them.’

Pochettino will find United no longer command the same spending power, for transfers and wages, as other top clubs, though their name still carries a cachet, if only they can be nimbler and smarter.

He will discover that one of the most godforsaken parts of the operation is the interminable decision-making process: multiple individuals sitting around the table whose opinions must be sought in rule by committee. Some of those who have been shown the door by Ratcliffe consider themselves well out of all that.

The individual United most need now is actually David Gill, the stellar chief executive who left in the same summer as Sir Alex Ferguson, 13 years ago.

Gill would bring a command and intellect way beyond the remotest comprehension of Berrada. He probably wouldn’t want the association with Ineos but nevertheless, United do need to find a proven, world-class chief executive officer. And a sporting director befitting the biggest club in the world.

In that interview with Mitten back in June, Berrada seemed very pleased with himself – sitting on a large sofa in a United meeting room with immaculately bright white adidas trainers and declaring that United had travelled a long way in 12 months.

‘I’m naturally optimistic by nature, although my wife says I should smile more,’ he said. ‘We’ve made some very difficult decisions, but they have put us where we are today.’

It was his 'aspiration’ to ‘make United great again’, he declared. He is a footnote to another unhappy chapter in the modern history of Manchester United, now. The monumental task lies at Pochettino’s door.

#1765. Gila explains how he went from ‘rock bottom’ at Lazio to joining Milan: “More kindness”

Mario Gila has explained how he managed to get through a difficult time at the start of his Italy adventure, eventually performing at such a high level that AC Milan decided to sign him.

Gila left Real Madrid and Spain in the summer of 2022, when he was just 21 years old, as Lazio secured his services. In his first season, however, he only got 765 minutes on the pitch and didn’t play a single game in the second half of the campaign.

The following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time. The growth only continued from there, resulting in Milan paying good money for him in the summer.

In his long interview with AC Milan for the interview series The Chamber, Gila discussed his initial struggles in Italy, hitting ‘rock bottom’ in his first season with Lazio. A psychologist and a changed mindset helped him get through it all.

When you make a mistake, are you very demanding and hard on yourself? I mean, how do you treat yourself when something doesn’t go the way you wanted?

“In the past, for example… I’ve changed a great deal. I went through a really difficult time early in my career here in Italy and hit rock bottom, but with outside help, psychological support, I got through it.

“That’s why I keep saying ‘before’. Back then, I was very hard on myself. I didn’t allow myself to fail. If I did, I was extremely negative towards myself, I couldn’t accept that I might fail or make mistakes.

“Now I handle it much better. Now I feel that making mistakes is part of the job, it’s something that helps you improve, something that helps you grow. So I deal with it much more calmly, I process it much better internally.

“I think you still need to hold yourself to high standards and you also need to know how to find a solution to that mistake, whether in your career or in your personal life, but with much more calm and more kindness towards myself.”

Regarding that difficult period you went through, which helped you grow and taught you so many things, you mentioned therapy. Could you tell me, not so much what happened, but what your experience with therapy was like? I mean, what did it give you at first?

“I sought help from a psychologist because I was going through a very difficult time and couldn’t find a way to move forward. We’re expected to deal with situations… that I find mentally overwhelming, at just 21 years old, when you have no professional experience, because in the end, everything comes at you so fast.

“So I went to a psychologist, and completely changed my perspective. I mean, I started seeing everything negative that happened to me as a step forward, thinking: this is something that will help you improve, something you needed to go through.

“Everything changed when I changed my perspective. I used to be very hard on myself, very hard, I demanded so much of myself. Now I’m someone who feels much more at ease.

“We can all fail, make mistakes, go through difficult situations, So the way I treat myself, the way I respond to myself, the way I talk to myself, I think it plays a crucial role in maintaining a consistently positive mindset.”

Pato is exactly the kind of transfer Liverpool need to steer clear of. Additionally, talks of an early exit from the club for Christian Benteke are ridiculous. The big Belgian has not had time to settle at the club, with his 17 appearances for the club being overseen by two different managers with different styles of playing, and both of these styles being vastly different from how he was played at Aston Villa last season. He deserves till the end of this season at the very least, if not more.

This is the a emergency signinga scenario — a situation all managers (and Boards) hope never arises. For a club with a relatively deep squad like Liverpool, injuries should be the last reason to sign a player, but there are exceptions. For example, the centre-half situation at Liverpool right now. When youai??i??re forced to play Jose Enrique and Tiago Ilori (who started his first competitive game of the season) as the centre-back pairing, the situation is truly dire. One could make a case for signing an experienced centre-half to step in, like Andrea Ranocchia (Inter Milan) and Neven Subotic (Borussia Dortmund), both of whom have been linked with a transfer to Liverpool FC.

Even in such an extreme scenario, seeing how Mamadou Sakho and Kolo Toure may possibly return within the week, these signings make no sense. You donai??i??t spend A?7 to A?10 million on players just to feature in a few games. Hopefully Liverpool FC will make it out of this window without any such expenditures.

History teaches us that short-cuts and quick-fixes can be accompanied by pretty massive pitfalls. Liverpool FC fans need to stop looking to the transfer market for the answers. Jurgen Klopp is at the helm, and his methods require investing time and effort in the players he works with. Heai??i??ll sign players when he comes across the right ones, but hopefully wonai??i??t be spending money searching for some unicorn signing that will miraculously fly the club to success.

And it is absolutely the right approach to take.

#1763. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1762. Corinthians vs Botafogo - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 16 Nov 2026 22:02

Relegation-threatened Corinthians will be looking to climb out of the Brasileirao drop zone when they welcome Copa Sudamericana hopefuls Botafogo to the Neo Quimica Arena this midweek..

The hosts sit 17th in the Brazilian top-flight table after 34 matches, one point behind 16th-placed Internacional, while the visitors are 12th and above 13th-placed Coritiba by virtue of goal difference.

Corinthians ended a 10-match winless league run with victory over Mirassol on matchday 33, and although they failed to secure back-to-back wins following their goalless draw at Sao Paulo last time out, taking a point from that encounter was still an impressive result for a side that had lost each of their previous five league away matches.

The result also means that the Timao have kept consecutive clean sheets after conceding in each of their previous 10 matches during that winless Brasileiro spell, reflecting the improvement in resilience since Clarence Seedorf took over the reins in October.

Fernando Diniz was sacked after the club suffered seven consecutive league defeats, before interim boss William Batista also lost to Palmeiras, but Corinthians have since recorded three results without defeat in four matches under Seedorf's guidance, with the only blemish being a 3-2 setback against Vasco da Gama on October 24.

Knowing that victory this midweek would lift his side temporarily out of the relegation zone, pending Internacional's game against Vasco later on, the former AC Milan midfielder will look to build on the fact that the Timao ended a five-match winless home league run with their victory over Mirassol.

Corinthians have now taken 22 points from their 17 matches at the Neo Quimica Arena in the top-flight campaign, a return that leaves the Sao Paulo-based team with the third-worst home record in the division.

Botafogo, meanwhile, head into this encounter looking to build on their 1-0 victory over Atletico-MG last time out, with Edenilson's 19th-minute goal proving decisive and lifting the Fire into the Copa Sudamericana zone.

The result also ended a two-match losing streak following defeats to Internacional and Remo, while marking Tite's second victory in seven games since his appointment in September and making him the club's third permanent manager of the season after the dismissals of Martin Anselmi and Franclim Carvalho.

Botafogo have now recorded 11 victories from their 34 league matches (D9, L14) this term, scoring 46 goals and conceding 53, meaning there is still room for improvement at both ends of the pitch.

Another victory could lift the Fire as high as 10th, depending on the results of 11th-placed Vasco and 10th-placed Sao Paulo, who both play on Thursday, although Wednesday's visitors are winless in each of their last six away games (D1, L5).

However, Botafogo can draw inspiration from the fact that they are unbeaten in their last five meetings with Corinthians and have recorded victories in three of those outings, including a 3-1 success in the most recent meeting between the two sides.

Corinthians will be without Yuri Alberto, Matheus Pereira and Andre Ramalho, with the first two suspended following their red cards last time out, while the latter is unavailable due to an accumulation of bookings.

Zakaria Labyad and Kayke remain long-term absentees with anterior cruciate ligament injuries, while Rodrigo Garro, Alex Santana, Raniele and former Arsenal defender Gabriel Paulista are working towards full fitness and remain doubtful.

André Luiz will also be unavailable for Corinthians after the CBF rejected the club's request to release him early from Brazil duty, with the midfielder set to remain with the national team for their friendly against Singapore on November 17, just a day before the clash with Botafogo.

Botafogo are expected to be without Nahuel Ferraresi, whose return from international duty could come too late for any major involvement, while Jordan Barrera is ruled out of the season with injury and Danilo is a doubt due to an adductor problem.

Arthur Chaves is still being assessed by the medical department, with Kaio Pantaleao also being targeted for a return after working towards full fitness.

H Souza; Matheuzinho, J Pedro, G Henrique, Angileri; Carrillo, Bidon; Kaio Cesar, Vitinho, Bidu; Depay

Batista; Vitinho, Justino, Marçal, Telles; C Medina, Edenilson; Ziyech, Montoro,  Martins; Soares

Corinthians have the greater need for points and should be motivated by the opportunity to move closer to safety, but their poor home record makes it difficult to back them to claim all three.

Botafogo have been inconsistent in recent weeks, yet their stronger league position and unbeaten run against the hosts suggest that Tite's side can leave Sao Paulo with a share of the points.

#1761. CorSport: RedBird could consider stock market listing of Milan’s new holding company

AC Milan’s new holding company, Milan Sports & Entertainment, could be publicly listed within five years according to a report.

Yesterday, RedBird announced the creation of a new holding company for the AC Milan project, named Milan Sports & Entertainment (MSE). The main goal is to have everything under one roof, from the football team to the new stadium and the NBA Europe project.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Cardinale himself said, there will be several new revenue streams that ultimately will benefit the football club, making it possible to invest more money in players and additional infrastructure. In short, it’s a big project and it could get even bigger.

According to Corriere dello Sport this morning, as cited by MilanNews, the launch of MSE proves that RedBird and Cardinale have a long-term plan for the club. A listing on the stock market cannot be ruled out within the next five years either, opening the company up to further investment.

Only two football clubs in Italy are publicly traded, namely Juventus and Lazio, meaning fans can effectively become shareholders. However, it should be noted that these shares rarely come with any real power, used more as a way of raising funds than anything else.

Outside of Italy, clubs like Borussia Dortmund and Manchester United are also publicly listed, so it’s not like Milan would be moving into uncharted territory.
